spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m3p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Hubs, Doors, MaxOpen, MaxTerm

\* Coordinator handover: a hub may vanish silently, so reservations are written to a
\* shared ledger (`granted`) instead of the acting hub's memory.
\* The successor therefore inherits the dead hub's promises and charges them to the cap.
\* The invariant guards the household policy limit on doors open-or-promised.

NoHub == "none"

VARIABLES coord, term, live, unlocked, granted
vars == <<coord, term, live, unlocked, granted>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ coord \in Hubs \cup {NoHub}
  /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
  /\ live \subseteq Hubs
  /\ unlocked \subseteq Doors
  /\ granted \subseteq Doors

Committed == unlocked \cup granted

Init ==
  /\ coord = NoHub
  /\ term = 0
  /\ live = Hubs
  /\ unlocked = {}
  /\ granted = {}

Elect(h) ==
  /\ h \in live
  /\ coord \notin live
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ coord' = h
  /\ UNCHANGED <<live, unlocked, granted>>

CrashSilently(h) ==
  /\ h \in live
  /\ Cardinality(live) > 1
  /\ live' = live \ {h}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coord, term, unlocked, granted>>

Reserve(d) ==
  /\ coord \in live
  /\ d \notin Committed
  /\ Cardinality(Committed) < MaxOpen
  /\ granted' = granted \cup {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coord, term, live, unlocked>>

OpenDoor(d) ==
  /\ d \in granted
  /\ unlocked' = unlocked \cup {d}
  /\ granted' = granted \ {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coord, term, live>>

Relock(d) ==
  /\ d \in unlocked
  /\ unlocked' = unlocked \ {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coord, term, live, granted>>

Revoke(d) ==
  /\ coord \in live
  /\ d \in granted
  /\ granted' = granted \ {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coord, term, live, unlocked>>

Next ==
  \/ \E h \in Hubs : Elect(h) \/ CrashSilently(h)
  \/ \E d \in Doors : Reserve(d) \/ OpenDoor(d) \/ Relock(d) \/ Revoke(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapacityHonored == Cardinality(Committed) <= MaxOpen
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Hubs = {"h1","h2","h3"}
  Doors = {"d1","d2","d3"}
  MaxOpen = 2
  MaxTerm = 3
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT CapacityHonored
nl:
A residential building manages its smart door locks through a small cluster of hub controllers. Each hub can drive any of the building's electronic locks, but at any moment only one hub is the acting coordinator. Coordination matters because the household security policy caps how many doors may stand open (or be promised to open) at the same time: an insurer-mandated limit that exists so a single compromised phone cannot fling the whole building open at once.

Unlocking is a two-step affair. The acting coordinator first writes a reservation for a door into a shared ledger that lives on the lock bus rather than in the coordinator's own memory. Only a door holding a reservation may actually be driven open. When the physical lock reports it has opened, the reservation is retired and the door moves into the open set. Closing a door returns it to the ordinary locked state. A coordinator may also revoke a reservation it no longer wants to honour, giving the capacity back without ever opening the door.

The failure mode this design must survive is a hub that dies silently: it stops answering, but it never announces its departure, and it may have already written reservations before it went quiet. The remaining hubs notice that the coordinator is no longer among the live hubs and elect a successor under a fresh, strictly higher term number. Because reservations were written to the shared ledger and not to the dead hub's memory, the successor inherits every outstanding reservation and counts it against the cap. The cluster keeps at least one hub alive; elections are only possible while a term number remains available.

The action set is exactly: elect a live hub as coordinator when the current coordinator is not live; crash a live hub silently while more than one hub remains live; reserve a door that is neither open nor already reserved, provided the cap has room; open a reserved door; relock an open door; and revoke an existing reservation.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of doors that are either standing open or holding an outstanding reservation never exceeds the building's configured cap, even across silent hub crashes and coordinator handovers.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od19m4p6t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Patrons, MaxSerial, Depths

\* Intake is a bounded FIFO whose depth limit is re-set at runtime; backpressure is
\* applied only at append time, so a shrink never evicts queued slips.
\* The head is always consumed -- granted when the card serial still matches, shredded
\* otherwise -- which is what keeps the queue from wedging on a dead slip.
\* The invariant guards against a hold surviving a suspension or a card reissue.

NoHold == MaxSerial + 1

VARIABLES intake, serial, privileged, hold, depth
vars == <<intake, serial, privileged, hold, depth>>

Slips == [pat : Patrons, sn : 0..MaxSerial]

TypeOK ==
  /\ intake \in Seq(Slips)
  /\ serial \in [Patrons -> 0..MaxSerial]
  /\ privileged \subseteq Patrons
  /\ hold \in [Patrons -> 0..(MaxSerial + 1)]
  /\ depth \in Depths

Queued(p) == \E i \in 1..Len(intake) : intake[i].pat = p

Init ==
  /\ intake = <<>>
  /\ serial = [p \in Patrons |-> 0]
  /\ privileged = Patrons
  /\ hold = [p \in Patrons |-> NoHold]
  /\ depth \in Depths

Submit(p) ==
  /\ ~Queued(p)
  /\ Len(intake) < depth
  /\ intake' = Append(intake, [pat |-> p, sn |-> serial[p]])
  /\ UNCHANGED <<serial, privileged, hold, depth>>

Grant ==
  /\ intake # <<>>
  /\ LET s == Head(intake) IN
       /\ s.pat \in privileged
       /\ s.sn = serial[s.pat]
       /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![s.pat] = s.sn]
  /\ intake' = Tail(intake)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<serial, privileged, depth>>

Shred ==
  /\ intake # <<>>
  /\ LET s == Head(intake) IN
       s.pat \notin privileged \/ s.sn # serial[s.pat]
  /\ intake' = Tail(intake)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<serial, privileged, hold, depth>>

ProcessHead == Grant \/ Shred

ReturnBook(p) ==
  /\ hold[p] # NoHold
  /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![p] = NoHold]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<intake, serial, privileged, depth>>

Suspend(p) ==
  /\ p \in privileged
  /\ privileged' = privileged \ {p}
  /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![p] = NoHold]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<intake, serial, depth>>

Reinstate(p) ==
  /\ p \notin privileged
  /\ privileged' = privileged \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<intake, serial, hold, depth>>

Reissue(p) ==
  /\ serial[p] < MaxSerial
  /\ serial' = [serial EXCEPT ![p] = serial[p] + 1]
  /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![p] = NoHold]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<intake, privileged, depth>>

Resize(d) ==
  /\ d \in Depths
  /\ d # depth
  /\ depth' = d
  /\ UNCHANGED <<intake, serial, privileged, hold>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Patrons : Submit(p) \/ ReturnBook(p) \/ Suspend(p) \/ Reinstate(p) \/ Reissue(p)
  \/ ProcessHead
  \/ \E d \in Depths : Resize(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(ProcessHead)

HoldsAreCurrent ==
  \A p \in Patrons :
    hold[p] # NoHold => (p \in privileged /\ hold[p] = serial[p])

SlipsDrain == \A p \in Patrons : Queued(p) ~> ~Queued(p)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Patrons = {"pa","pb","pc"}
  MaxSerial = 1
  Depths = {1,2}
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT HoldsAreCurrent
PROPERTY SlipsDrain
nl:
A public library runs its hold-and-pickup service through a single intake queue. When a patron asks to reserve a title, the request is appended to the intake queue together with a snapshot of the serial number currently printed on that patron's library card. The queue is deliberately bounded: the circulation desk will refuse to append a new request once the queue has reached its current depth limit, and patrons simply have to come back later. That depth limit is not fixed. A supervising librarian raises it during term-paper season and lowers it again in the quiet weeks, so the bound the desk enforces changes while requests are already sitting in the queue. Lowering the limit never discards anything already queued; it only stops new arrivals until the backlog drains.

Two things can invalidate a queued request before the clerk reaches it. A patron's borrowing privileges can be suspended for unpaid fines, and a patron who reports a lost card is issued a replacement with a fresh serial number. Pickup is performed against the physical card, so a request written under an old serial number can no longer be honoured by anyone. The clerk therefore examines only the head of the queue: if the head belongs to a patron whose privileges are intact and whose card serial still matches the snapshot taken at submission time, the clerk hands over the book and records the hold under that serial number. Otherwise the clerk shreds the slip and moves on. Either way the head leaves the queue, so the desk never wedges on a dead request.

Holds already granted are also affected. Suspending a patron confiscates any book currently on hold for them, and reissuing a card voids the hold that was tied to the old serial. A patron may return a held book at any time, and a suspended patron may be reinstated once the fines are settled.

The action set is exactly: submit a request for a patron who has no request already queued, while the queue is shorter than the current depth limit; process the head of the queue by either granting a hold (fresh serial, privileges intact) or shredding it; return a held book; suspend an active patron, voiding any hold; reinstate a suspended patron; reissue a patron's card with the next serial number, voiding any hold; and change the depth limit to any configured value.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a patron is recorded as holding a book, that patron's privileges are intact and the serial number the hold was granted under is still the serial number on that patron's current card.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every request that reaches the intake queue eventually leaves it, either honoured as a hold or shredded as stale, so no patron's slip sits in the queue forever.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m4p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Blocks, Depths, RegisterSize

\* Commissioning orders flow through a FIFO whose depth limit is re-set while running;
\* backpressure is applied only when pushing, so a shrink never drops queued orders.
\* Breaking a block's seal is irreversible and is recorded in an append-only register.
\* The invariant is the pipeline-exclusion fact that makes a second commissioning
\* of an already-registered block unreachable.

VARIABLES orders, register, ready, faulted, depth
vars == <<orders, register, ready, faulted, depth>>

Commissioned == { register[i] : i \in 1..Len(register) }
Queued(b) == \E i \in 1..Len(orders) : orders[i] = b

TypeOK ==
  /\ orders \in Seq(Blocks)
  /\ register \in Seq(Blocks)
  /\ ready \subseteq Blocks
  /\ faulted \subseteq Blocks
  /\ depth \in Depths

Init ==
  /\ orders = <<>>
  /\ register = <<>>
  /\ ready = {}
  /\ faulted = {}
  /\ depth \in Depths

WorkFinished(b) ==
  /\ b \notin ready
  /\ b \notin faulted
  /\ b \notin Commissioned
  /\ ~Queued(b)
  /\ ready' = ready \cup {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<orders, register, faulted, depth>>

Push(b) ==
  /\ b \in ready
  /\ Len(orders) < depth
  /\ orders' = Append(orders, b)
  /\ ready' = ready \ {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<register, faulted, depth>>

Commission ==
  /\ orders # <<>>
  /\ Len(register) < RegisterSize
  /\ Head(orders) \notin Commissioned
  /\ register' = Append(register, Head(orders))
  /\ orders' = Tail(orders)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ready, faulted, depth>>

FinalCheckFails ==
  /\ orders # <<>>
  /\ faulted' = faulted \cup {Head(orders)}
  /\ orders' = Tail(orders)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<register, ready, depth>>

Repair(b) ==
  /\ b \in faulted
  /\ b \notin Commissioned
  /\ faulted' = faulted \ {b}
  /\ ready' = ready \cup {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<orders, register, depth>>

Retune(d) ==
  /\ d \in Depths
  /\ d # depth
  /\ depth' = d
  /\ UNCHANGED <<orders, register, ready, faulted>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Blocks : WorkFinished(b) \/ Push(b) \/ Repair(b)
  \/ Commission
  \/ FinalCheckFails
  \/ \E d \in Depths : Retune(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SealsAreFinal ==
  \A b \in Commissioned : b \notin ready /\ b \notin faulted /\ ~Queued(b)
====
nl:
A metro line is divided into fixed signalling blocks. After a block has been taken out of service for track work, it cannot simply be handed back to traffic: the control centre must commission it, which means breaking the tamper seal on the block's safety certificate and writing the block into the line's permanent commissioning register. Breaking a seal is irreversible. A certificate can never be re-sealed, and the regulator treats a second register entry for the same block as evidence that the first commissioning was never real, so a duplicate entry is a reportable incident rather than a harmless retry.

Commissioning orders travel through a bounded dispatch queue. When the maintenance gang finishes work on a block, the block becomes ready, and a dispatcher may push a commissioning order for it onto the queue. The queue applies backpressure: no new order is accepted once the queue has reached the depth limit currently in force. That depth limit is adjusted while the system runs, because the control centre allows a deeper backlog during the overnight engineering window than it does during service hours. Shrinking the limit never throws away orders that are already queued; it only stalls new pushes until the backlog works down.

The controller works strictly from the head of the queue. If the block at the head still has an unbroken seal, the controller commissions it: the seal is broken and the block's identifier is appended to the commissioning register. If the block instead fails its final check at the head of the queue, the order is torn up and the block is marked faulted, which sends it back to the gang; a faulted block can be repaired and become ready again, but only if it has not already been commissioned. The register has a fixed physical size and the control centre stops commissioning when it is full.

The action set is exactly: mark a block ready when it is not already ready, faulted, queued, or commissioned; push a commissioning order for a ready block onto the queue while the queue is below the current depth limit, removing it from the ready set; commission the block at the head of the queue when its seal is unbroken and the register has room; fail the final check on the head of the queue, marking that block faulted; repair a faulted block back to ready provided it has not been commissioned; and change the queue depth limit to another configured value.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A block whose identifier already appears in the commissioning register is never simultaneously sitting in the dispatch queue, in the ready set, or in the faulted set, so no second commissioning order for it can ever reach the head of the queue.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od12m5p5t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Units, Sites, MaxRounds

\* Every release is authorised by a strict majority of transfusion sites.
\* A site may be behind (cannot vote) but never fails: it always catches up,
\* which is what makes each open ballot reach quorum eventually.
\* The invariant is that release is one-way: an issued unit has no live ballot.

VARIABLES balloting, votes, issued, behind, rounds
vars == <<balloting, votes, issued, behind, rounds>>

HasQuorum(u) == 2 * Cardinality(votes[u]) > Cardinality(Sites)

TypeOK ==
  /\ balloting \subseteq Units
  /\ votes \in [Units -> SUBSET Sites]
  /\ issued \subseteq Units
  /\ behind \subseteq Sites
  /\ rounds \in [Units -> 0..MaxRounds]

Init ==
  /\ balloting = {}
  /\ votes = [u \in Units |-> {}]
  /\ issued = {}
  /\ behind = {}
  /\ rounds = [u \in Units |-> 0]

OpenBallot(u) ==
  /\ u \notin balloting
  /\ u \notin issued
  /\ rounds[u] < MaxRounds
  /\ balloting' = balloting \cup {u}
  /\ rounds' = [rounds EXCEPT ![u] = rounds[u] + 1]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![u] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<issued, behind>>

CastVote(s, u) ==
  /\ u \in balloting
  /\ s \notin behind
  /\ s \notin votes[u]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![u] = votes[u] \cup {s}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<balloting, issued, behind, rounds>>

ReleaseUnit(u) ==
  /\ u \in balloting
  /\ HasQuorum(u)
  /\ issued' = issued \cup {u}
  /\ balloting' = balloting \ {u}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, behind, rounds>>

FallBehind(s) ==
  /\ s \notin behind
  /\ behind' = behind \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<balloting, votes, issued, rounds>>

CatchUp(s) ==
  /\ s \in behind
  /\ behind' = behind \ {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<balloting, votes, issued, rounds>>

Reconcile ==
  /\ behind # {}
  /\ behind' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<balloting, votes, issued, rounds>>

SomeVote == \E s \in Sites, u \in Units : CastVote(s, u)
SomeRelease == \E u \in Units : ReleaseUnit(u)

Next ==
  \/ \E u \in Units : OpenBallot(u) \/ ReleaseUnit(u)
  \/ \E s \in Sites, u \in Units : CastVote(s, u)
  \/ \E s \in Sites : FallBehind(s) \/ CatchUp(s)
  \/ Reconcile

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(Reconcile)
  /\ SF_vars(SomeVote)
  /\ WF_vars(SomeRelease)

ReleaseIsOneWay == \A u \in issued : u \notin balloting

BallotsReachQuorum == \A u \in Units : (u \in balloting) ~> (u \in issued)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Units = {"u1","u2"}
  Sites = {"s1","s2","s3"}
  MaxRounds = 1
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ReleaseIsOneWay
PROPERTY BallotsReachQuorum
nl:
A regional blood bank keeps its rare-phenotype units in a shared cold store, and every release of a unit to an operating theatre is authorised collectively by the region's transfusion sites rather than by whoever happens to be at the fridge. Releasing a unit is irreversible: once a unit leaves the cold chain it can never be returned to inventory, and the regional registry treats a unit as permanently gone the moment the release is recorded.

Authorisation works by ballot. A site opens a release ballot for a specific unit; opening a ballot assigns it a fresh round number and clears any votes carried over from an earlier round. Each site independently checks the crossmatch paperwork and casts its yes-vote into the ballot. When strictly more than half of the sites have voted, the ballot has a quorum and the unit may be released: the unit is recorded as issued and the ballot is closed. A ballot may only be opened for a unit that has not already been issued, and a unit's ballot may only be opened a limited number of times before the regional registry refuses further rounds.

Sites in this region are slow, not unreliable. A site can fall behind — its paperwork terminal queues up, its technician is in theatre, its link to the registry is congested — and while it is behind it cannot cast a vote. But no site ever fails outright. Individual sites do sometimes catch up on their own, and in addition the registry runs a reconciliation pass that brings every lagging site current in one sweep, so a period in which sites are behind is always followed by a period in which they can vote again. This is what lets the region promise that authorisation is a matter of delay rather than of deadlock.

The action set is exactly: open a release ballot for a unit that is neither already balloting nor already issued, provided the unit has rounds remaining; cast a site's vote into an open ballot when that site is not behind and has not already voted in this round; release a unit whose open ballot has reached quorum, recording it as issued and closing the ballot; put a site behind; bring a single behind site back up to date; and run the reconciliation sweep that clears every behind site at once.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No unit that has already been issued has an open release ballot, so a second quorum for an already-released unit can never form.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every release ballot that is opened eventually reaches quorum and its unit is issued, because the reconciliation sweep always returns lagging sites to service and the outstanding votes then get cast.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od11m4p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Jobs, MaxSheets, Ceiling

\* The print bus gives no ordering guarantee, so the inbox and the streaming stage are
\* modelled as unordered sets: any pending request may be picked next.
\* Backpressure is the admit/bounce choice, re-evaluated against live commitment.
\* The invariant guards a weighted ceiling (sheets, not job count) over every stage
\* the spooler has taken responsibility for.

VARIABLES sheets, inbox, streaming, spooled, onPress
vars == <<sheets, inbox, streaming, spooled, onPress>>

Committed == streaming \cup spooled \cup onPress

SheetLoad(S) ==
  LET tot[T \in SUBSET Jobs] ==
        IF T = {} THEN 0
        ELSE LET j == CHOOSE x \in T : TRUE IN sheets[j] + tot[T \ {j}]
  IN tot[S]

TypeOK ==
  /\ sheets \in [Jobs -> 1..MaxSheets]
  /\ inbox \subseteq Jobs
  /\ streaming \subseteq Jobs
  /\ spooled \subseteq Jobs
  /\ onPress \subseteq Jobs

Init ==
  /\ sheets \in [Jobs -> 1..MaxSheets]
  /\ inbox = {}
  /\ streaming = {}
  /\ spooled = {}
  /\ onPress = {}

SubmitJob(j) ==
  /\ j \notin inbox
  /\ j \notin Committed
  /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {j}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sheets, streaming, spooled, onPress>>

AdmitJob(j) ==
  /\ j \in inbox
  /\ SheetLoad(Committed \cup {j}) =< Ceiling
  /\ inbox' = inbox \ {j}
  /\ streaming' = streaming \cup {j}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sheets, spooled, onPress>>

BounceJob(j) ==
  /\ j \in inbox
  /\ SheetLoad(Committed \cup {j}) > Ceiling
  /\ inbox' = inbox \ {j}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sheets, streaming, spooled, onPress>>

StreamDone(j) ==
  /\ j \in streaming
  /\ streaming' = streaming \ {j}
  /\ spooled' = spooled \cup {j}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sheets, inbox, onPress>>

Mount(j) ==
  /\ j \in spooled
  /\ onPress = {}
  /\ spooled' = spooled \ {j}
  /\ onPress' = {j}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sheets, inbox, streaming>>

CompleteRun(j) ==
  /\ j \in onPress
  /\ onPress' = onPress \ {j}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sheets, inbox, streaming, spooled>>

Next ==
  \E j \in Jobs :
    SubmitJob(j) \/ AdmitJob(j) \/ BounceJob(j)
      \/ StreamDone(j) \/ Mount(j) \/ CompleteRun(j)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SheetCeilingHonored == SheetLoad(Committed) =< Ceiling
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Jobs = {"j1","j2","j3"}
  MaxSheets = 2
  Ceiling = 3
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT SheetCeilingHonored
nl:
A commercial print shop runs one large press fed by a spooler. Every job that arrives has a fixed sheet count, decided when the customer's file is prepared and unchanged thereafter. What the spooler must protect is not the number of jobs but the amount of paper committed at once: the shop's finishing line can only absorb a fixed number of sheets of work-in-progress, so the total sheet count of everything the spooler has taken responsibility for must stay within that ceiling.

Requests reach the spooler over a shared print bus, and the bus makes no ordering promises. Submissions land in an unordered inbox and the spooler may look at them in any order; likewise, once a job has been admitted, its actual page data streams in over the same bus and jobs finish streaming in an order unrelated to the order in which they were admitted. A spec that decided admission based on the order requests were sent would be wrong here, so the spooler re-evaluates the sheet ceiling at the moment it admits a job, counting everything it is already committed to: jobs admitted but still streaming, jobs fully spooled to disk, and the job currently mounted on the press.

Backpressure is explicit. When the spooler picks a request out of the inbox it either admits it, if the ceiling still has room for that job's sheets, or bounces it back to the customer, if it does not. A bounced request simply disappears from the inbox; the customer is free to submit it again later, and by then the press may well have freed up room. Admitted jobs stream in, then get mounted on the press one at a time, then complete and release their sheets.

The action set is exactly: submit a job that is neither in the inbox nor already committed anywhere in the pipeline; admit a job from the inbox when the sheet ceiling can still cover it; bounce a job from the inbox when it cannot; finish streaming an admitted job so it becomes fully spooled; mount a spooled job on the press; and complete the job on the press, releasing its sheets.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total sheet count of all jobs the spooler is committed to — still streaming, fully spooled, or on the press — never exceeds the shop's work-in-progress sheet ceiling.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od19m6p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Copies, Patrons, LeaseTicks

\* A copy is offered under a lease with a countdown; a patron who goes quiet never
\* announces it, so only the countdown can free the copy again.
\* Collection is one-way: it discharges the patron's reservation coupon and removes
\* the copy from the shelf. The invariant is that a discharged coupon has left every
\* place from which a second collection could be started.

Unoffered == "unoffered"

VARIABLES shelf, lease, clock, waiting, discharged, quiet
vars == <<shelf, lease, clock, waiting, discharged, quiet>>

Stale == { c \in Copies : lease[c] # Unoffered /\ clock[c] = 0 }

TypeOK ==
  /\ shelf \subseteq Copies
  /\ lease \in [Copies -> Patrons \cup {Unoffered}]
  /\ clock \in [Copies -> 0..LeaseTicks]
  /\ waiting \subseteq Patrons
  /\ discharged \subseteq Patrons
  /\ quiet \subseteq Patrons

Init ==
  /\ shelf = Copies
  /\ lease = [c \in Copies |-> Unoffered]
  /\ clock = [c \in Copies |-> 0]
  /\ waiting = {}
  /\ discharged = {}
  /\ quiet = {}

Reserve(p) ==
  /\ p \notin waiting
  /\ p \notin discharged
  /\ \A c \in Copies : lease[c] # p
  /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, lease, clock, discharged, quiet>>

OfferCopy(c, p) ==
  /\ c \in shelf
  /\ lease[c] = Unoffered
  /\ p \in waiting
  /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![c] = p]
  /\ clock' = [clock EXCEPT ![c] = LeaseTicks]
  /\ waiting' = waiting \ {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, discharged, quiet>>

TickTimer ==
  /\ \E c \in Copies : lease[c] # Unoffered /\ clock[c] > 0
  /\ clock' = [c \in Copies |->
                 IF lease[c] # Unoffered /\ clock[c] > 0 THEN clock[c] - 1 ELSE clock[c]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, lease, waiting, discharged, quiet>>

SweepLapsed ==
  /\ Stale # {}
  /\ lease' = [c \in Copies |-> IF c \in Stale THEN Unoffered ELSE lease[c]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, clock, waiting, discharged, quiet>>

Collect(c) ==
  /\ lease[c] # Unoffered
  /\ clock[c] > 0
  /\ lease[c] \notin quiet
  /\ discharged' = discharged \cup {lease[c]}
  /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![c] = Unoffered]
  /\ shelf' = shelf \ {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, waiting, quiet>>

GoQuiet(p) ==
  /\ p \notin quiet
  /\ quiet' = quiet \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, lease, clock, waiting, discharged>>

Resurface(p) ==
  /\ p \in quiet
  /\ quiet' = quiet \ {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, lease, clock, waiting, discharged>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Patrons : Reserve(p) \/ GoQuiet(p) \/ Resurface(p)
  \/ \E c \in Copies, p \in Patrons : OfferCopy(c, p)
  \/ \E c \in Copies : Collect(c)
  \/ TickTimer
  \/ SweepLapsed

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(TickTimer) /\ WF_vars(SweepLapsed)

CouponsDischargeOnce ==
  \A p \in discharged : p \notin waiting /\ (\A c \in Copies : lease[c] # p)

LeasesAlwaysEnd ==
  \A c \in Copies : (lease[c] # Unoffered) ~> (lease[c] = Unoffered)
====

CONSTANTS
  Copies = {"c1","c2"}
  Patrons = {"pa","pb"}
  LeaseTicks = 1
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT CouponsDischargeOnce
PROPERTY LeasesAlwaysEnd
nl:
A branch library runs a reserve shelf behind the circulation desk. A patron who wants a title that is currently out places a reservation; when a copy becomes free it is moved onto the reserve shelf and offered to one waiting patron. An offer is a lease with a clock on it: the copy is held under that patron's name for a fixed number of ticks of the desk's shift timer and no longer. While the lease is running the patron may come in and collect.

Collection is the irreversible step. When the patron collects, the copy leaves the reserve shelf for good — it is charged to the patron's account and the reservation coupon that entitled them to it is discharged. A discharged coupon is not reissued: the patron is no longer on the waiting list, holds no offer, and cannot place the same reservation again in this cycle. This is deliberate, because the branch's audit reconciles collected copies against discharged coupons one-for-one, and a coupon that got discharged twice would mean a copy left the building without a matching record.

The failure mode the lease exists for is a patron who goes quiet. Someone places a reservation, gets an offer, and then simply stops responding — the phone number is dead, they moved away, they forgot. They never announce this; from the desk's point of view the offer is simply not being collected. A quiet patron cannot collect, and the desk has no way of knowing whether a silent patron is gone for good or will resurface later. The lease clock is what stops such a patron from pinning a copy forever: the shift timer ticks down every running lease, and when a lease reaches zero the desk sweeps it, pulling the copy back onto the shelf as unoffered so it can go to somebody else. The patron whose offer lapsed drops off the list and would have to place the reservation again.

The action set is exactly: place a reservation for a patron who is not already waiting, not holding an offer, and whose coupon has not been discharged; offer an unoffered shelf copy to a waiting patron, starting that copy's lease clock at full and taking the patron off the waiting list; tick the shift timer, decrementing every running lease clock that has not yet reached zero; sweep every lease whose clock has reached zero, returning those copies to the shelf as unoffered; collect a copy whose lease is still running, by a patron who has not gone quiet, discharging that patron's coupon and taking the copy off the shelf permanently; have a patron go quiet; and have a quiet patron resurface, once a new contact number finally reaches the desk.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A patron whose reservation coupon has been discharged is never on the waiting list and never holds a lease on any copy, so no coupon can be discharged a second time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every lease that starts eventually ends — the copy is either collected or swept back onto the shelf — so no offer to a patron who has gone quiet can hold a copy forever.

---- MODULE W4Od10m5p6t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Interlockings, Routes, MaxConfig

\* The panel that votes is resized while the line runs, so the majority threshold
\* itself moves; reconfiguration bumps the configuration number, cancels every
\* cleared route and discards every vote taken under the old panel.
\* The invariant rejects authority backed by decommissioned or unsynchronised units.

VARIABLES config, panel, unitConfig, votes, cleared
vars == <<config, panel, unitConfig, votes, cleared>>

Majority(r) == 2 * Cardinality(votes[r]) > Cardinality(panel)

TypeOK ==
  /\ config \in 0..MaxConfig
  /\ panel \subseteq Interlockings
  /\ unitConfig \in [Interlockings -> 0..MaxConfig]
  /\ votes \in [Routes -> SUBSET Interlockings]
  /\ cleared \subseteq Routes

Init ==
  /\ config = 0
  /\ panel = Interlockings
  /\ unitConfig = [i \in Interlockings |-> 0]
  /\ votes = [r \in Routes |-> {}]
  /\ cleared = {}

Reconfigure(g) ==
  /\ g # {}
  /\ g # panel
  /\ config < MaxConfig
  /\ config' = config + 1
  /\ panel' = g
  /\ votes' = [r \in Routes |-> {}]
  /\ cleared' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED unitConfig

Resync(i) ==
  /\ unitConfig[i] < config
  /\ unitConfig' = [unitConfig EXCEPT ![i] = config]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<config, panel, votes, cleared>>

CastVote(i, r) ==
  /\ i \in panel
  /\ unitConfig[i] = config
  /\ r \notin cleared
  /\ i \notin votes[r]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![r] = votes[r] \cup {i}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<config, panel, unitConfig, cleared>>

ClearRoute(r) ==
  /\ r \notin cleared
  /\ Majority(r)
  /\ cleared' = cleared \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<config, panel, unitConfig, votes>>

CancelRoute(r) ==
  /\ r \in cleared
  /\ cleared' = cleared \ {r}
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![r] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<config, panel, unitConfig>>

Next ==
  \/ \E g \in SUBSET Interlockings : Reconfigure(g)
  \/ \E i \in Interlockings : Resync(i)
  \/ \E i \in Interlockings, r \in Routes : CastVote(i, r)
  \/ \E r \in Routes : ClearRoute(r) \/ CancelRoute(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AuthorityIsCurrent ==
  \A r \in cleared :
    /\ votes[r] \subseteq panel
    /\ \A i \in votes[r] : unitConfig[i] = config
    /\ Majority(r)
====
nl:
A metro line's signalling is done by a panel of interlocking computers. Before a train may be given a movement authority over a route, a strict majority of the panel must vote for it: each interlocking independently checks track circuits, point positions and conflicting routes, and casts its vote. Only when the votes on a route exceed half the panel is the route cleared and the authority handed to the train.

What makes this interesting is that the panel is not a fixed set. Interlockings are commissioned and decommissioned while the line is in service — a spare is brought online for the peak, a unit is taken out for a firmware change, a depot extension adds a new one. Each such change is a reconfiguration: it publishes a new configuration under a strictly higher configuration number and names the new panel. Because the size of the panel is exactly what determines how many votes a majority takes, changing the panel changes the threshold under everyone's feet. Reconfiguration therefore also cancels every movement authority currently outstanding and throws away every vote cast under the old configuration; routes must be re-voted from scratch under the new panel.

An interlocking learns about a reconfiguration by resynchronising, which brings its own configuration number up to the published one. Until it resynchronises it is running superseded logic — its view of which points are motorised and which routes conflict may simply be wrong — so its vote must not be counted. An interlocking that has been decommissioned is no longer in the panel at all and its vote must not be counted either, whatever configuration number it thinks it is running. A cleared route can be cancelled by the controller, which also discards the votes that cleared it.

The action set is exactly: reconfigure to a different non-empty panel under the next configuration number, cancelling all cleared routes and discarding all votes; resynchronise an interlocking whose configuration number is behind the published one; cast a vote on a route that is not already cleared, from an interlocking that is in the current panel, is running the current configuration, and has not already voted on that route; clear a route whose votes exceed half the current panel; and cancel a cleared route, discarding its votes.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every route currently holding a movement authority is backed by a set of votes drawn entirely from the currently commissioned panel, cast only by interlockings running the current configuration number, and larger than half of that panel.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od6m8p1t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Controllers, Cars, MaxRevision

\* Two independently built dispatch controllers share one pool of car records.
\* Amendments are read-modify-write, so the spec tracks the revision each controller
\* read as the basis of its pending write; the coarse pool claim then the fine per-car
\* claim are what keep that basis from going stale under it.
\* The invariant is the no-lost-update condition, not an exclusion claim.

Free == "free"
Nothing == "nothing"

VARIABLES poolClaim, carClaim, staged, basis, revision
vars == <<poolClaim, carClaim, staged, basis, revision>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ poolClaim \in Controllers \cup {Free}
  /\ carClaim \in [Cars -> Controllers \cup {Free}]
  /\ staged \in [Controllers -> Cars \cup {Nothing}]
  /\ basis \in [Controllers -> 0..MaxRevision]
  /\ revision \in [Cars -> 0..MaxRevision]

Init ==
  /\ poolClaim = Free
  /\ carClaim = [c \in Cars |-> Free]
  /\ staged = [k \in Controllers |-> Nothing]
  /\ basis = [k \in Controllers |-> 0]
  /\ revision = [c \in Cars |-> 0]

TakePool(k) ==
  /\ poolClaim = Free
  /\ poolClaim' = k
  /\ UNCHANGED <<carClaim, staged, basis, revision>>

DropPool(k) ==
  /\ poolClaim = k
  /\ poolClaim' = Free
  /\ UNCHANGED <<carClaim, staged, basis, revision>>

StageAmend(k, c) ==
  /\ poolClaim = k
  /\ staged[k] = Nothing
  /\ carClaim[c] = Free
  /\ revision[c] < MaxRevision
  /\ carClaim' = [carClaim EXCEPT ![c] = k]
  /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![k] = c]
  /\ basis' = [basis EXCEPT ![k] = revision[c]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<poolClaim, revision>>

WriteBack(k) ==
  /\ staged[k] # Nothing
  /\ LET c == staged[k] IN
       /\ revision' = [revision EXCEPT ![c] = basis[k] + 1]
       /\ carClaim' = [carClaim EXCEPT ![c] = Free]
  /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![k] = Nothing]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<poolClaim, basis>>

Abandon(k) ==
  /\ staged[k] # Nothing
  /\ carClaim' = [carClaim EXCEPT ![staged[k]] = Free]
  /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![k] = Nothing]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<poolClaim, basis, revision>>

SomeWriteBack == \E k \in Controllers : WriteBack(k)

Next ==
  \/ \E k \in Controllers : TakePool(k) \/ DropPool(k) \/ WriteBack(k) \/ Abandon(k)
  \/ \E k \in Controllers, c \in Cars : StageAmend(k, c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(SomeWriteBack)

BasisNeverGoesStale ==
  \A k \in Controllers :
    staged[k] # Nothing => basis[k] = revision[staged[k]]

StagedWorkResolves ==
  \A k \in Controllers : (staged[k] # Nothing) ~> (staged[k] = Nothing)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Controllers = {"lowrise","highrise"}
  Cars = {"carA","carB"}
  MaxRevision = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT BasisNeverGoesStale
PROPERTY StagedWorkResolves
nl:
A skyscraper is served by two dispatch controllers — the low-rise controller and the high-rise controller — which were installed by different vendors at different times and know nothing about each other's internals. After a refit they were wired to a single shared pool of cars, so both now write into the same per-car assignment record. Each record holds the car's current call list together with a revision number that the record's own hardware stamps on every accepted write.

Amending a car's assignment is a read-modify-write. The controller reads the record, notes the revision it read, works out the new call list, and writes it back stamped with the next revision. The danger the refit introduced is the classic one: if both controllers read revision n and both write revision n+1, one controller's amendment is silently thrown away — a floor call vanishes and a passenger waits for a car that is never coming. Nothing about the record hardware prevents that; the discipline has to come from outside.

The discipline is a two-level claim. To touch anything, a controller must first take the pool-wide claim, of which there is one. Holding the pool claim, it may then take the per-car claim on one specific car and read that car's record, which stages an amendment: the controller remembers the revision it read as the basis for its write. Having staged, it releases the pool claim so the other controller can get on with a different car, but it keeps the per-car claim until it writes. Writing back bumps the record's revision to one past the basis and releases the per-car claim. A controller may also give up on a staged amendment without writing, releasing the per-car claim and leaving the revision alone. A controller stages at most one amendment at a time, and the record hardware refuses to go past its maximum revision, so a controller only stages against a record that still has room to advance.

The action set is exactly: take the pool-wide claim when it is free; release the pool-wide claim; stage an amendment by taking a free per-car claim while holding the pool claim, on a car whose revision has not reached the maximum, when the controller has nothing staged; write back a staged amendment, bumping the record's revision past the basis and releasing the per-car claim; and abandon a staged amendment, releasing the per-car claim without changing the revision.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a controller has an amendment staged, the basis revision it read is still the record's current revision, so no write can ever be built on a revision that another controller has already superseded.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every staged amendment is eventually resolved — the controller either writes it back or abandons it — so a staged amendment never pins a car's record indefinitely.

---- MODULE W4Od15m2p1t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Engines, Shards, Orders

\* Two independently built engines install whole-book images into one shared record.
\* Two-phase commit: a shard's yes-vote both binds the shard to that engine and
\* certifies that the proposed image has not fallen behind the shared book.
\* The invariant is the no-lost-update condition at the point of no return -- a fully
\* voted transaction cannot be about to erase an order the book already holds.

Uncommitted == "uncommitted"

VARIABLES book, image, inflight, yesVotes, boundTo
vars == <<book, image, inflight, yesVotes, boundTo>>

FullyVoted(e) == e \in inflight /\ yesVotes[e] = Shards

TypeOK ==
  /\ book \subseteq Orders
  /\ image \in [Engines -> SUBSET Orders]
  /\ inflight \subseteq Engines
  /\ yesVotes \in [Engines -> SUBSET Shards]
  /\ boundTo \in [Shards -> Engines \cup {Uncommitted}]

Init ==
  /\ book = {}
  /\ image = [e \in Engines |-> {}]
  /\ inflight = {}
  /\ yesVotes = [e \in Engines |-> {}]
  /\ boundTo = [s \in Shards |-> Uncommitted]

Unbind(e) == [s \in Shards |-> IF boundTo[s] = e THEN Uncommitted ELSE boundTo[s]]

BeginAmend(e, o) ==
  /\ e \notin inflight
  /\ o \notin book
  /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {e}
  /\ image' = [image EXCEPT ![e] = book \cup {o}]
  /\ yesVotes' = [yesVotes EXCEPT ![e] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<book, boundTo>>

GrantVote(e, s) ==
  /\ e \in inflight
  /\ boundTo[s] = Uncommitted
  /\ book \subseteq image[e]
  /\ boundTo' = [boundTo EXCEPT ![s] = e]
  /\ yesVotes' = [yesVotes EXCEPT ![e] = yesVotes[e] \cup {s}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<book, image, inflight>>

RefuseVote(e) ==
  /\ e \in inflight
  /\ ~(book \subseteq image[e])
  /\ inflight' = inflight \ {e}
  /\ boundTo' = Unbind(e)
  /\ yesVotes' = [yesVotes EXCEPT ![e] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<book, image>>

CommitAmend(e) ==
  /\ FullyVoted(e)
  /\ book' = image[e]
  /\ inflight' = inflight \ {e}
  /\ boundTo' = Unbind(e)
  /\ yesVotes' = [yesVotes EXCEPT ![e] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED image

AbandonAmend(e) ==
  /\ e \in inflight
  /\ inflight' = inflight \ {e}
  /\ boundTo' = Unbind(e)
  /\ yesVotes' = [yesVotes EXCEPT ![e] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<book, image>>

CancelOrder(o) ==
  /\ inflight = {}
  /\ o \in book
  /\ book' = book \ {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<image, inflight, yesVotes, boundTo>>

Next ==
  \/ \E e \in Engines, o \in Orders : BeginAmend(e, o)
  \/ \E e \in Engines, s \in Shards : GrantVote(e, s)
  \/ \E e \in Engines : RefuseVote(e) \/ CommitAmend(e) \/ AbandonAmend(e)
  \/ \E o \in Orders : CancelOrder(o)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoAmendmentErasesTheBook ==
  \A e \in Engines : FullyVoted(e) => book \subseteq image[e]
====
nl:
Before the market opens, an exchange runs an opening auction whose order book is a single shared record. Two matching engines write into it: the lit engine that handles ordinary member flow and the auction engine that handles the crossing session. They were built years apart by different teams and neither knows how the other works internally; the refit that merged the two sessions simply pointed both at the same book.

An amendment to the book is prepared as a complete replacement image. An engine that wants to add an order reads the current book, builds the image it intends to install — the book as it read it, plus the new order — and then runs a two-phase commit across the exchange's order-book shards. In the voting phase the engine asks each shard in turn. A shard that is not already committed to another engine's transaction inspects the proposed image and votes yes only if that image still contains everything the shared book currently contains; if the image has fallen behind, the shard refuses and the transaction is torn down. A shard that votes yes is committed to that engine and will not vote for anybody else until the transaction finishes. When every shard has voted yes, the engine commits: the proposed image becomes the book, and every shard the engine was holding is released. An engine may also abandon its transaction at any point, releasing whatever shards it holds.

The hazard this exists to prevent is the ordinary lost update. Both engines read the same book, both build an image from it, and if both were allowed to install their image, whichever installs second silently erases the other's order. An order that a member believes is in the auction but which is not in the book is an unwinnable dispute for the exchange, so the shard vote is the only thing standing between the two engines and that outcome. Orders may also be cancelled outright, but only while the book is quiescent — when neither engine has a transaction in flight.

The action set is exactly: begin an amendment for an engine with nothing in flight, adding an order that is not already in the book and fixing the proposed image; grant a shard's yes-vote to an in-flight engine when the shard is uncommitted and the proposed image still covers the current book; refuse a shard's vote and tear down the transaction when the proposed image no longer covers the book; commit an engine's amendment once every shard has voted yes, installing the image and releasing the shards; abandon an in-flight transaction, releasing its shards; and cancel an order out of the book while no transaction is in flight.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever an engine has collected a yes-vote from every shard, the image it is about to install still contains every order currently in the shared book, so committing it cannot erase another engine's order.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od19m4p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Titles, Cubbies, QueueMax

\* Intake is a bounded FIFO; the clerk always consumes the front, filing it if a cubby
\* is free and bouncing it otherwise, which is what makes backpressure temporary.
\* Slip (title -> cubby) and index (cubby -> title) are kept as separate variables
\* on purpose: the invariant is their agreement, and disagreement is exactly the
\* double-filing of one cubby that loses a book.

NoCubby == "nocubby"
NoTitle == "notitle"

VARIABLES intake, slip, index, bounced, urgent
vars == <<intake, slip, index, bounced, urgent>>

InQueue(t) == \E i \in 1..Len(intake) : intake[i] = t
FreeCubby == { c \in Cubbies : index[c] = NoTitle }

TypeOK ==
  /\ intake \in Seq(Titles)
  /\ slip \in [Titles -> Cubbies \cup {NoCubby}]
  /\ index \in [Cubbies -> Titles \cup {NoTitle}]
  /\ bounced \subseteq Titles
  /\ urgent \subseteq Titles

Init ==
  /\ intake = <<>>
  /\ slip = [t \in Titles |-> NoCubby]
  /\ index = [c \in Cubbies |-> NoTitle]
  /\ bounced = {}
  /\ urgent = {}

QueueTitle(t) ==
  /\ ~InQueue(t)
  /\ slip[t] = NoCubby
  /\ t \notin bounced
  /\ Len(intake) < QueueMax
  /\ intake' = Append(intake, t)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slip, index, bounced, urgent>>

FileHead ==
  /\ intake # <<>>
  /\ FreeCubby # {}
  /\ \E c \in FreeCubby :
       /\ slip' = [slip EXCEPT ![Head(intake)] = c]
       /\ index' = [index EXCEPT ![c] = Head(intake)]
  /\ intake' = Tail(intake)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bounced, urgent>>

BounceHead ==
  /\ intake # <<>>
  /\ FreeCubby = {}
  /\ bounced' = bounced \cup {Head(intake)}
  /\ intake' = Tail(intake)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slip, index, urgent>>

ClerkStep == FileHead \/ BounceHead

Requeue(t) ==
  /\ t \in bounced
  /\ bounced' = bounced \ {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<intake, slip, index, urgent>>

Collect(t) ==
  /\ slip[t] # NoCubby
  /\ index' = [index EXCEPT ![slip[t]] = NoTitle]
  /\ slip' = [slip EXCEPT ![t] = NoCubby]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<intake, bounced, urgent>>

FlagUrgent(t) ==
  /\ t \notin urgent
  /\ urgent' = urgent \cup {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<intake, slip, index, bounced>>

OverrideFile(t, c) ==
  /\ t \in urgent
  /\ slip[t] = NoCubby
  /\ index[c] = NoTitle
  /\ slip' = [slip EXCEPT ![t] = c]
  /\ index' = [index EXCEPT ![c] = t]
  /\ intake' = SelectSeq(intake, LAMBDA x : x # t)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bounced, urgent>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Titles : QueueTitle(t) \/ Requeue(t) \/ Collect(t) \/ FlagUrgent(t)
  \/ \E t \in Titles, c \in Cubbies : OverrideFile(t, c)
  \/ ClerkStep

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(ClerkStep)

SlipAndIndexAgree ==
  \A t \in Titles : slip[t] # NoCubby => index[slip[t]] = t

BackpressureLifts ==
  (Len(intake) = QueueMax) ~> (Len(intake) < QueueMax)
====

CONSTANTS
  Titles = {"t1","t2","t3"}
  Cubbies = {"k1","k2"}
  QueueMax = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT SlipAndIndexAgree
PROPERTY BackpressureLifts
nl:
The pickup shelf at a busy library branch is divided into numbered cubbies. When a reserved title comes in, it has to be put somewhere a patron can find it, and the branch's whole retrieval workflow depends on two things staying in agreement: the slip stapled to the book, which says which cubby the book went into, and the shelf index at the desk, which says which book is in each cubby. If those two ever disagree — if a book's slip points at a cubby that the index says holds a different book — then two books have been filed into one cubby and one of them is, for practical purposes, lost.

Incoming titles are handled through a short intake queue. A title that is not already queued, not already shelved, and not sitting in the bounced pile can be added to the queue while the queue is below its depth limit; once the queue is full the desk simply refuses new intake until the clerk works some off. The clerk always deals with the front of the queue. If a cubby is free, the title goes into it and both the slip and the index are written. If every cubby is occupied, the title is bounced instead, and it goes onto the bounced pile from which it can be re-queued later. Either way the front of the queue is consumed, so a full queue always drains.

The branch manager has an override. She can flag a title as urgent — an interlibrary loan going back tomorrow, a reserve for a course that starts in the morning — and a flagged title can be filed straight into a free cubby without waiting its turn, which also pulls it out of the intake queue if it happens to be sitting there. The override skips the queue but not the cubby discipline: she still has to pick a cubby that the index says is empty, and she still writes both the slip and the index. Patrons collect books, which empties the cubby and clears the slip.

The action set is exactly: queue a title that is unqueued, unshelved and not bounced, while the queue is below its depth limit; file the front of the queue into a free cubby, writing slip and index; bounce the front of the queue onto the bounced pile when no cubby is free; re-queue a bounced title by taking it off the pile; collect a shelved title, emptying its cubby and clearing its slip; flag a title as urgent; and use the manager's override to file a flagged, unshelved title directly into an empty cubby, removing it from the intake queue if present.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every title whose slip names a cubby, the shelf index for that cubby names that same title, so no two titles are ever filed into the same cubby.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever the intake queue is at its depth limit and intake is being refused, the queue eventually drops below the limit again, so backpressure at this desk is always temporary.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od5m2p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Players, TeamSize

\* Match formation is two-phase: invite a team, collect acceptances, then commit.
\* Acceptances arrive in any order, so they are held as an unordered set rather than
\* a sequence; any outstanding invitee may be the next to reply.
\* The invariant is conservation of the roster: lobby, held and playing partition it.

VARIABLES lobby, held, playing, invited, accepted
vars == <<lobby, held, playing, invited, accepted>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ lobby \subseteq Players
  /\ held \subseteq Players
  /\ playing \subseteq Players
  /\ invited \subseteq Players
  /\ accepted \subseteq Players

Init ==
  /\ lobby = Players
  /\ held = {}
  /\ playing = {}
  /\ invited = {}
  /\ accepted = {}

Propose(S) ==
  /\ invited = {}
  /\ S \subseteq lobby
  /\ Cardinality(S) = TeamSize
  /\ invited' = S
  /\ accepted' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lobby, held, playing>>

AcceptSeat(p) ==
  /\ p \in invited
  /\ p \notin accepted
  /\ p \in lobby
  /\ accepted' = accepted \cup {p}
  /\ lobby' = lobby \ {p}
  /\ held' = held \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<playing, invited>>

TearDown ==
  /\ invited # {}
  /\ lobby' = lobby \cup accepted
  /\ held' = held \ accepted
  /\ invited' = {}
  /\ accepted' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED playing

Decline(p) ==
  /\ p \in invited
  /\ p \notin accepted
  /\ TearDown

TimeOut == TearDown

CommitMatch ==
  /\ invited # {}
  /\ accepted = invited
  /\ held' = held \ accepted
  /\ playing' = playing \cup accepted
  /\ invited' = {}
  /\ accepted' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED lobby

LeaveMatch(p) ==
  /\ p \in playing
  /\ playing' = playing \ {p}
  /\ lobby' = lobby \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<held, invited, accepted>>

Next ==
  \/ \E S \in SUBSET Players : Propose(S)

CONSTANTS
  Players = {"p1","p2","p3","p4"}
  TeamSize = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT RosterConserved
nl:
An online shooter runs a lobby matchmaker. Every player connected to the region is in exactly one of three situations: sitting in the lobby waiting for a game, holding a seat in a match that is being formed, or actually playing. The matchmaker's whole job is to move players between those three situations without ever losing one or cloning one. A player who ends up in neither the lobby nor a match has fallen off the service and will sit staring at a loading screen; a player who somehow appears both in the lobby and in a live match gets matched into a second game while already shooting in the first, which the anti-cheat treats as an exploit.

Forming a match is a two-phase commit with the players' clients as the participants. The matchmaker picks a full team's worth of players out of the lobby and invites them; each invited client is asked to hold a seat. A client that accepts moves its player out of the lobby and into the held state, and its acceptance is recorded. The matchmaker only commits the match once every invited client has accepted, at which point all the held players become playing. If any invited client declines, or if the matchmaker gives up waiting, the attempt is torn down and every player who was holding a seat for that attempt goes straight back to the lobby.

The lobby's network is a best-effort mesh and it does not preserve ordering. Acceptances come back in whatever order the routing happens to deliver them, which need not be the order the invitations went out, and the matchmaker must not assume otherwise: it works from the set of acceptances it has, not from a sequence. That is why acceptance is modelled as an unordered collection and any outstanding invitee may be the next to reply.

The action set is exactly: propose a match by inviting a full team's worth of lobby players when no attempt is in flight; record an acceptance from any outstanding invitee, moving that player out of the lobby into the held state; decline from any outstanding invitee, which tears the attempt down and returns every held player of that attempt to the lobby; commit the attempt once every invitee has accepted, moving all its held players into play; time the attempt out, returning its held players to the lobby; and have a playing player leave their match back to the lobby.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The lobby, the set of players holding seats, and the set of players in a live match always partition the region's player roster — every player is in exactly one of the three, so no player is ever lost or duplicated by a match attempt.

---- MODULE W4Od19m9p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Branches, Titles, MaxEpoch, Pages, FirstAuthority

\* The authority to append is assigned per epoch and that assignment is never rewritten.
\* A branch that crashed silently comes back still believing its old epoch, so appends
\* carry the writer's believed epoch and are refused unless it is the published one.
\* The invariant audits the ledger: correct author for the stamped epoch, and stamps
\* that never run backwards down the pages.

Unassigned == "unassigned"

VARIABLES epoch, authorityOf, believed, down, ledger
vars == <<epoch, authorityOf, believed, down, ledger>>

Entries == [ti : Titles, ep : 0..MaxEpoch, by : Branches]
Reserved(t) == \E i \in 1..Len(ledger) : ledger[i].ti = t

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ authorityOf \in [0..MaxEpoch -> Branches \cup {Unassigned}]
  /\ believed \in [Branches -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ down \subseteq Branches
  /\ ledger \in Seq(Entries)

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ authorityOf = [e \in 0..MaxEpoch |-> IF e = 0 THEN FirstAuthority ELSE Unassigned]
  /\ believed = [b \in Branches |-> 0]
  /\ down = {}
  /\ ledger = <<>>

Reconfigure(b) ==
  /\ b \notin down
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ authorityOf' = [authorityOf EXCEPT ![epoch + 1] = b]
  /\ believed' = [believed EXCEPT ![b] = epoch + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<down, ledger>>

GossipRound ==
  /\ \E b \in Branches : b \notin down /\ believed[b] # epoch
  /\ believed' = [b \in Branches |-> IF b \in down THEN believed[b] ELSE epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, authorityOf, down, ledger>>

CrashSilently(b) ==
  /\ b \notin down
  /\ down' = down \cup {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, authorityOf, believed, ledger>>

Recover(b) ==
  /\ b \in down
  /\ down' = down \ {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, authorityOf, believed, ledger>>

AppendReservation(b, t) ==
  /\ b \notin down
  /\ authorityOf[epoch] = b
  /\ believed[b] = epoch
  /\ ~Reserved(t)
  /\ Len(ledger) < Pages
  /\ ledger' = Append(ledger, [ti |-> t, ep |-> believed[b], by |-> b])
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, authorityOf, believed, down>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Branches : Reconfigure(b) \/ CrashSilently(b) \/ Recover(b)
  \/ \E b \in Branches, t \in Titles : AppendReservation(b, t)
  \/ GossipRound

Converged == \A b \in Branches : b \notin down => believed[b] = epoch

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(GossipRound)

LedgerAuditsClean ==
  /\ \A i \in 1..Len(ledger) : authorityOf[ledger[i].ep] = ledger[i].by
  /\ \A i \in 1..(Len(ledger) - 1) : ledger[i].ep =< ledger[i + 1].ep

EpochBeliefConverges == (~Converged) ~> Converged
====

CONSTANTS
  Branches = {"north","south"}
  Titles = {"t1","t2"}
  MaxEpoch = 1
  Pages = 2
  FirstAuthority = "north"
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT LedgerAuditsClean
PROPERTY EpochBeliefConverges
nl:
A consortium of library branches shares one reservation ledger. Reservations are not written by whoever takes the phone call: at any moment exactly one branch holds the reservation authority, and only that branch appends to the ledger. The authority is assigned by epoch-numbered reconfiguration. When the consortium reconfigures, it moves to the next epoch number and names the branch that will hold the authority for that epoch; the epoch-to-branch assignment for an epoch is fixed once and never rewritten, which is what makes the ledger auditable years later.

Branches do not all learn about a reconfiguration at the same time. Each branch carries the epoch number it currently believes is in force, and it stamps that number onto anything it writes. A branch that is behind can be brought up to date, and the consortium periodically runs a gossip round that brings every branch that is currently up to the published epoch in one pass.

Branches also fail, and they fail silently: a branch's server simply stops answering, with no notice to anyone, and it may come back hours later still believing the epoch it believed when it died. That is the dangerous case. A recovered branch that was the authority two epochs ago may well try to append a reservation stamped with its stale epoch number, and if the ledger accepted it the audit trail would show a reservation authorised by a branch that had already been superseded, out of order with everything appended since. Appends are therefore refused unless the appending branch is the authority for the currently published epoch, is up, and believes the currently published epoch. Reconfiguration itself may only be initiated by a branch that is up, and the branch that takes the authority learns the new epoch as part of taking it. The ledger has a fixed number of pages.

The action set is exactly: reconfigure to the next epoch, naming an up branch as the new authority and bringing that branch's believed epoch up to date; run a gossip round that sets every up branch's believed epoch to the published one; crash a branch silently; recover a crashed branch with its believed epoch untouched; and append a reservation for an unreserved title, stamped with the appending branch's believed epoch and name, when that branch is up and is the authority for the published epoch.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every entry in the reservation ledger names, as its author, the branch that was assigned the authority for the epoch stamped on that entry, and the stamped epochs never decrease as the ledger is read from first page to last.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever some branch that is up believes an epoch other than the published one, the consortium eventually reaches a state in which every up branch believes the published epoch.

---- MODULE W4Od4m5p2t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cars, BeltLength, Sensors, OverrideBudget

\* Each advance of the chain needs a strict majority of the sensor votes; the manager's
\* key card can force one without a majority, out of a bounded budget.
\* Both kinds of advance shift the chain identically, which is the point: the invariant
\* is the vehicle census, and the override must not be able to break it.

Clear == "clear"
Positions == 1..BeltLength

VARIABLES belt, forecourt, apron, votes, budget
vars == <<belt, forecourt, apron, votes, budget>>

OnBelt == { c \in Cars : \E s \in Positions : belt[s] = c }
Majority == 2 * Cardinality(votes) > Cardinality(Sensors)

TypeOK ==
  /\ belt \in [Positions -> Cars \cup {Clear}]
  /\ forecourt \subseteq Cars
  /\ apron \subseteq Cars
  /\ votes \subseteq Sensors
  /\ budget \in 0..OverrideBudget

Init ==
  /\ belt = [s \in Positions |-> Clear]
  /\ forecourt = {}
  /\ apron = {}
  /\ votes = {}
  /\ budget = OverrideBudget

ShiftChain ==
  /\ belt' = [s \in Positions |-> IF s = 1 THEN Clear ELSE belt[s - 1]]
  /\ apron' = IF belt[BeltLength] = Clear THEN apron ELSE apron \cup {belt[BeltLength]}
  /\ votes' = {}

Arrive(c) ==
  /\ c \notin forecourt
  /\ c \notin OnBelt
  /\ c \notin apron
  /\ forecourt' = forecourt \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<belt, apron, votes, budget>>

CastVote(s) ==
  /\ s \notin votes
  /\ votes' = votes \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<belt, forecourt, apron, budget>>

VotedAdvance ==
  /\ Majority
  /\ ShiftChain
  /\ UNCHANGED <<forecourt, budget>>

ForcedAdvance ==
  /\ budget > 0
  /\ budget' = budget - 1
  /\ ShiftChain
  /\ UNCHANGED forecourt

LoadCar(c) ==
  /\ c \in forecourt
  /\ belt[1] = Clear
  /\ belt' = [belt EXCEPT ![1] = c]
  /\ forecourt' = forecourt \ {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<apron, votes, budget>>

DriveAway(c) ==
  /\ c \in apron
  /\ apron' = apron \ {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<belt, forecourt, votes, budget>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Arrive(c) \/ LoadCar(c) \/ DriveAway(c)
  \/ \E s \in Sensors : CastVote(s)
  \/ VotedAdvance
  \/ ForcedAdvance

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

VehicleCensusHolds ==
  /\ forecourt \cap OnBelt = {}
  /\ forecourt \cap apron = {}
  /\ OnBelt \cap apron = {}
  /\ \A s1, s2 \in Positions : (s1 # s2 /\ belt[s1] # Clear) => belt[s1] # belt[s2]
====

CONSTANTS
  Cars = {"c1","c2","c3"}
  BeltLength = 2
  Sensors = {"s1","s2","s3"}
  OverrideBudget = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT VehicleCensusHolds
nl:
An automatic car wash moves vehicles through the tunnel on a chain conveyor divided into numbered positions. A car waits in the forecourt, is loaded onto the first position when that position is clear, rides the conveyor one position at a time, and is pushed off the far end into the exit apron, where its driver eventually collects it and drives away. The site's whole accounting rests on knowing where every vehicle on the premises is: a car that the system thinks is nowhere has effectively been lost inside the tunnel, and a car the system thinks is at two positions at once means the conveyor has been double-counted and the next vehicle will be loaded on top of somebody's bonnet.

Advancing the conveyor is not a decision any single component is allowed to make. Position sensors, the brush-pressure monitor and the dryer interlock each vote on whether the chain may move; the chain advances only once a strict majority of them has voted for the current advance. Once the chain moves, all outstanding votes are discarded and the sensors must vote again for the next advance.

The shift manager carries a key card that overrides the vote. When a sensor has failed dirty and the tunnel is backing up, she can force a single advance without a majority. The override is not free: the key card allows only a limited number of forced advances per shift and every use is logged for the site's insurer. What the override does not change is the physical bookkeeping — a forced advance moves the chain exactly the way a voted advance does, pushing the car at the far end onto the exit apron and clearing the first position.

The action set is exactly: a car arrives in the forecourt if it is not already on the premises; a sensor casts its vote for the current advance; the conveyor advances when a strict majority of sensors has voted, discarding the votes; the manager forces an advance without a majority while her override budget lasts, also discarding the votes; a waiting car is loaded onto the first conveyor position when that position is clear; and a car on the exit apron is driven away, leaving the premises.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The forecourt, the conveyor and the exit apron always account for every vehicle on the premises exactly once — no vehicle is in two of them at once, no vehicle occupies two conveyor positions, and no vehicle on the premises is unaccounted for.

---- MODULE W4Od19m2p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Requests, Branches, ShelfSpaces, HomeBranch

\* Two-phase commit across branches; a branch that crashes silently just stops voting,
\* so a request can sit prepared and in doubt while holding a shelf space.
\* A prepared request already consumes a space, so the capacity test is applied when a
\* request is logged as prepared, and it counts reserved spaces as well as occupied ones.

VARIABLES stage, target, voted, logged, offline
vars == <<stage, target, voted, logged, offline>>

Stages == {"idle", "voting", "prepared", "committed"}
Occupying(b) == { r \in Requests : target[r] = b /\ stage[r] \in {"prepared", "committed"} }

TypeOK ==
  /\ stage \in [Requests -> Stages]
  /\ target \in [Requests -> Branches]
  /\ voted \in [Requests -> SUBSET Branches]
  /\ logged \subseteq Requests
  /\ offline \subseteq Branches

Init ==
  /\ stage = [r \in Requests |-> "idle"]
  /\ target = [r \in Requests |-> HomeBranch]
  /\ voted = [r \in Requests |-> {}]
  /\ logged = {}
  /\ offline = {}

BeginRequest(r, b) ==
  /\ stage[r] = "idle"
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![r] = "voting"]
  /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![r] = b]
  /\ voted' = [voted EXCEPT ![r] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<logged, offline>>

RecordVote(r, b) ==
  /\ stage[r] = "voting"
  /\ b \notin offline
  /\ b \notin voted[r]
  /\ voted' = [voted EXCEPT ![r] = voted[r] \cup {b}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, target, logged, offline>>

MakePrepared(r) ==
  /\ stage[r] = "voting"
  /\ Branches \ offline \subseteq voted[r]
  /\ Cardinality(Occupying(target[r])) < ShelfSpaces
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![r] = "prepared"]
  /\ logged' = logged \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<target, voted, offline>>

CommitOne(r) ==
  /\ stage[r] = "prepared"
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![r] = "committed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<target, voted, logged, offline>>

InDoubtSweep ==
  /\ \E r \in Requests : stage[r] = "prepared" /\ r \in logged
  /\ stage' = [r \in Requests |->
                 IF stage[r] = "prepared" /\ r \in logged THEN "committed" ELSE stage[r]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<target, voted, logged, offline>>

Abandon(r) ==
  /\ stage[r] \in {"voting", "prepared"}
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]
  /\ voted' = [voted EXCEPT ![r] = {}]
  /\ logged' = logged \ {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<target, offline>>

CollectVolume(r) ==
  /\ stage[r] = "committed"
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]
  /\ voted' = [voted EXCEPT ![r] = {}]
  /\ logged' = logged \ {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<target, offline>>

GoOffline(b) ==
  /\ b \notin offline
  /\ offline' = offline \cup {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, target, voted, logged>>

ComeOnline(b) ==
  /\ b \in offline
  /\ offline' = offline \ {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, target, voted, logged>>

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Requests, b \in Branches : BeginRequest(r, b) \/ RecordVote(r, b)
  \/ \E r \in Requests : MakePrepared(r) \/ CommitOne(r) \/ Abandon(r) \/ CollectVolume(r)
  \/ \E b \in Branches : GoOffline(b) \/ ComeOnline(b)
  \/ InDoubtSweep

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(InDoubtSweep)

ShelfSpacesRespected ==
  \A b \in Branches : Cardinality(Occupying(b)) =< ShelfSpaces

NoPermanentDoubt ==
  \A r \in Requests : (stage[r] = "prepared") ~> (stage[r] # "prepared")
====

CONSTANTS
  Requests = {"r1","r2","r3"}
  Branches = {"east","west"}
  ShelfSpaces = 2
  HomeBranch = "east"
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ShelfSpacesRespected
PROPERTY NoPermanentDoubt
nl:
A regional library consortium runs interlibrary loans. When a patron at one branch asks for a title held elsewhere, the request has to be committed jointly: the lending branch must agree to release the volume, the receiving branch must agree to take custody of it, and both must agree before anything physically moves. The consortium therefore runs each request as a two-phase commit across the branches. The request starts idle, goes out for voting, and each branch that is up records its vote. Once every branch that is currently up has voted, the request is written into the consortium's recovery log and becomes prepared.

Becoming prepared is the moment that costs something. Each branch keeps a holding shelf behind its desk for interlibrary volumes that are inbound or waiting to be collected, and that shelf has a fixed number of spaces. A request that is prepared has already reserved a space on its destination branch's holding shelf, and a request that has been committed occupies one for real. The consortium therefore refuses to let a request become prepared unless the destination branch's shelf can still take it, counting both the reserved spaces and the occupied ones. A patron collecting their volume frees the space again.

Branches crash silently. A branch's desk system goes offline without warning and without telling anybody, and while it is offline it casts no votes; requests in voting simply wait for the branches that are still up. The awkward consequence is that a request can sit prepared indefinitely — in doubt, holding a shelf space, with nobody to hand the volume to. The consortium's recovery manager exists for exactly this: it holds the log and periodically runs an in-doubt sweep that commits every prepared request in the log at once, whether or not the branches involved are currently reachable. Requests may also be committed one at a time on the normal path, and a request that has not yet been committed may be abandoned, returning it to idle and giving back whatever it had reserved.

The action set is exactly: begin an idle request, naming its destination branch and putting it out for voting; record a vote from a branch that is up and has not yet voted; make a request prepared once every up branch has voted, logging it, provided the destination shelf still has a space counting reserved and occupied; commit a prepared request on the normal path; run the recovery manager's in-doubt sweep, committing every prepared logged request at once; abandon a request that is voting or prepared, returning it to idle; collect a committed volume, freeing its shelf space; crash a branch silently; and bring a crashed branch back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every branch, the number of interlibrary requests that have reserved or are occupying a space on that branch's holding shelf never exceeds the number of spaces that shelf has.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: A request that becomes prepared never stays in doubt forever — it eventually leaves the prepared state, because the recovery manager's in-doubt sweep always runs.

---- MODULE W4Od18m1p5t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Locks, NumHubs, WorkOrderMax

\* The ring token says who may drive a burn; a busy hub keeps the token rather than
\* dropping out, so slowness only delays the ring.
\* Burning a one-time key slot is irreversible, and it can happen either from the hubs'
\* work order or by hand at the door panel; the invariant ties the burn records to the
\* physical slots and keeps a burned lock off the work order.

Hubs == 1..NumHubs
NoBurner == 0
Installer == NumHubs + 1

VARIABLES token, workOrder, spent, burnedBy, busy
vars == <<token, workOrder, spent, burnedBy, busy>>

NextHub(h) == IF h = NumHubs THEN 1 ELSE h + 1
Scheduled(l) == \E i \in 1..Len(workOrder) : workOrder[i] = l

TypeOK ==
  /\ token \in Hubs
  /\ workOrder \in Seq(Locks)
  /\ spent \subseteq Locks
  /\ burnedBy \in [Locks -> 0..(NumHubs + 1)]
  /\ busy \subseteq Hubs

Init ==
  /\ token = 1
  /\ workOrder = <<>>
  /\ spent = {}
  /\ burnedBy = [l \in Locks |-> NoBurner]
  /\ busy = {}

PassToken ==
  /\ token \notin busy
  /\ token' = NextHub(token)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<workOrder, spent, burnedBy, busy>>

GetBusy(h) ==
  /\ h \notin busy
  /\ busy' = busy \cup {h}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, workOrder, spent, burnedBy>>

FinishUp(h) ==
  /\ h \in busy
  /\ busy' = busy \ {h}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, workOrder, spent, burnedBy>>

ScheduleLock(l) ==
  /\ l \notin spent
  /\ ~Scheduled(l)
  /\ Len(workOrder) < WorkOrderMax
  /\ workOrder' = Append(workOrder, l)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, spent, burnedBy, busy>>

BurnFront ==
  /\ workOrder # <<>>
  /\ Head(workOrder) \notin spent
  /\ spent' = spent \cup {Head(workOrder)}
  /\ burnedBy' = [burnedBy EXCEPT ![Head(workOrder)] = token]
  /\ workOrder' = Tail(workOrder)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, busy>>

HandBurn(l) ==
  /\ l \notin spent
  /\ ~Scheduled(l)
  /\ spent' = spent \cup {l}
  /\ burnedBy' = [burnedBy EXCEPT ![l] = Installer]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, workOrder, busy>>

Next ==
  \/ PassToken
  \/ \E h \in Hubs : GetBusy(h) \/ FinishUp(h)
  \/ \E l \in Locks : ScheduleLock(l) \/ HandBurn(l)
  \/ BurnFront

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BurnRecordsAreFinal ==
  \A l \in Locks :
    /\ (l \in spent) <=> (burnedBy[l] # NoBurner)
    /\ (burnedBy[l] # NoBurner) => ~Scheduled(l)
====

CONSTANTS
  Locks = {"front","back","garage"}
  NumHubs = 3
  WorkOrderMax = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT BurnRecordsAreFinal
nl:
A smart-home installation has several hub controllers wired into a ring, and a set of electronic door locks. Each lock ships with a one-time-programmable key slot: the household master key can be burned into the slot exactly once, and after that the slot is spent. There is no erase. A lock whose slot has been spent still works, but it can never be re-keyed, so a second burn attempt is not merely wasteful — it is the event the installer's audit is designed to catch, because it means the hub believed a lock was unkeyed when it was not.

Only the hub currently holding the ring token may drive a burn, and the token moves round the ring one hop at a time. The hubs share a work order: a short list of locks scheduled to be keyed. The token holder may add a lock to the work order if the lock's slot is still fresh and the lock is not already on the list, and the token holder may burn the lock at the front of the work order, which spends that lock's slot, writes the holder's identity into the lock's burn record, and takes the lock off the front of the list.

The hubs in this installation are slow, not broken. A hub that is busy — running a firmware check, waiting on a congested radio channel, mid-way through a scene update — will hang on to the token rather than passing it on, and the ring simply waits. It always finishes eventually and passes the token along; no hub ever drops off the ring or loses the token. Slowness therefore costs latency, not correctness.

There is one other way a slot gets spent. An installer standing at the door panel can burn a lock by hand. Because the installer cannot see the hubs' work order and the hubs cannot see the installer, hand burning is only permitted on a lock the hubs have not scheduled; that restriction is what keeps the two routes from racing for the same slot. A hand burn also writes a burn record, naming the installer rather than a hub.

The action set is exactly: pass the token one hop round the ring, provided the current holder is not busy; make a hub busy; let a busy hub finish and stop being busy; schedule a lock onto the work order, by the token holder, when the lock's slot is fresh and the lock is not already scheduled; burn the lock at the front of the work order, by the token holder, spending its slot and writing the burn record; and hand burn an unscheduled lock with a fresh slot at the door panel, writing an installer burn record.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A lock has a burn record if and only if its key slot is spent, and any lock with a burn record is absent from the hubs' work order, so no lock can ever be presented for a second burn.
