---- MODULE W4Od12m5p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Depots, TotalStock, StartDepot

\* Transfers are executed only on a strict majority of depot votes; votes are kept as a
\* set because the store-and-forward network delivers them in any order.
\* An idle proposal is encoded as an amount of zero.
\* The invariant is the regulator's arithmetic: shelves plus quarantine plus vans is
\* always exactly the accountable stock, whatever the network reordered.

VARIABLES shelf, quarantine, van, offer, votes
vars == <<shelf, quarantine, van, offer, votes>>

Tally(f) ==
  LET g[S \in SUBSET Depots] ==
        IF S = {} THEN 0
        ELSE LET d == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN f[d] + g[S \ {d}]
  IN g[Depots]

Majority == 2 * Cardinality(votes) > Cardinality(Depots)

TypeOK ==
  /\ shelf \in [Depots -> 0..TotalStock]
  /\ quarantine \in [Depots -> 0..TotalStock]
  /\ van \in [Depots -> 0..TotalStock]
  /\ offer \in [src : Depots, dst : Depots, amt : 0..TotalStock]
  /\ votes \subseteq Depots

Init ==
  /\ shelf = [d \in Depots |-> IF d = StartDepot THEN TotalStock ELSE 0]
  /\ quarantine = [d \in Depots |-> 0]
  /\ van = [d \in Depots |-> 0]
  /\ offer = [src |-> StartDepot, dst |-> StartDepot, amt |-> 0]
  /\ votes = {}

ProposeMove(f, t, n) ==
  /\ offer.amt = 0
  /\ f # t
  /\ n > 0
  /\ n =< shelf[f]
  /\ offer' = [src |-> f, dst |-> t, amt |-> n]
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, quarantine, van>>

CastVote(d) ==
  /\ offer.amt > 0
  /\ d \notin votes
  /\ votes' = votes \cup {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, quarantine, van, offer>>

ExecuteMove ==
  /\ offer.amt > 0
  /\ Majority
  /\ offer.amt =< shelf[offer.src]
  /\ shelf' = [shelf EXCEPT ![offer.src] = shelf[offer.src] - offer.amt]
  /\ van' = [van EXCEPT ![offer.dst] = van[offer.dst] + offer.amt]
  /\ offer' = [offer EXCEPT !.amt = 0]
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED quarantine

DropOffer ==
  /\ offer.amt > 0
  /\ offer' = [offer EXCEPT !.amt = 0]
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, quarantine, van>>

Unload(d) ==
  /\ van[d] > 0
  /\ shelf' = [shelf EXCEPT ![d] = shelf[d] + van[d]]
  /\ van' = [van EXCEPT ![d] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<quarantine, offer, votes>>

NightlyRound ==
  /\ \E d \in Depots : van[d] > 0
  /\ shelf' = [d \in Depots |-> shelf[d] + van[d]]
  /\ van' = [d \in Depots |-> 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<quarantine, offer, votes>>

Hold(d, n) ==
  /\ n > 0
  /\ n =< shelf[d]
  /\ shelf' = [shelf EXCEPT ![d] = shelf[d] - n]
  /\ quarantine' = [quarantine EXCEPT ![d] = quarantine[d] + n]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<van, offer, votes>>

ReleaseHold(d, n) ==
  /\ n > 0
  /\ n =< quarantine[d]
  /\ quarantine' = [quarantine EXCEPT ![d] = quarantine[d] - n]
  /\ shelf' = [shelf EXCEPT ![d] = shelf[d] + n]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<van, offer, votes>>

Next ==
  \/ \E f, t \in Depots, n \in 1..TotalStock : ProposeMove(f, t, n)
  \/ \E d \in Depots : CastVote(d) \/ Unload(d)
  \/ \E d \in Depots, n \in 1..TotalStock : Hold(d, n) \/ ReleaseHold(d, n)
  \/ ExecuteMove
  \/ DropOffer
  \/ NightlyRound

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(NightlyRound)

StockArithmeticCloses ==
  Tally(shelf) + Tally(quarantine) + Tally(van) = TotalStock

  (\E d \in Depots : van[d] > 0) ~> (\A d \in Depots : van[d] = 0)

CONSTANTS
  Depots = {"da","db","dc"}
  TotalStock = 3
  StartDepot = "da"
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT StockArithmeticCloses
PROPERTY VansAlwaysUnload
nl:
A regional blood service tracks its plasma stock in whole donation units. Every unit the service owns is in exactly one of three places: on the shelf at one of the depots, in quarantine at a depot pending a repeat screening result, or on a van somewhere between depots. The service's regulator does not care where a unit is on any given day, but it cares enormously that the arithmetic closes: the total across shelves, quarantine and vans must always equal the stock the service is accountable for. A unit that goes missing from the count is a unit that cannot be traced to a recipient, and a unit that appears from nowhere means a transfer was double-counted.

Moving stock between depots is not a unilateral decision. A depot proposes a transfer — so many units, from this depot to that one — and the depots then vote on it. The proposal is only executed once strictly more than half the depots have voted for it, at which point the units leave the sending depot's shelf and go onto the van as stock in transit to the destination. A proposal can also be dropped without executing, which discards the votes.

The depots communicate over a store-and-forward network that makes no ordering promise at all. Votes on a proposal are collected as a set, not as a sequence: they arrive in whatever order the network happens to deliver them and the proposer must not assume the order it sent the requests in. The same is true of arrivals — vans are unloaded at whichever depot happens to have a free bay first, so the receipt of stock in transit is not tied to the order in which shipments were dispatched. To stop stock sitting on vans indefinitely, the service also runs a nightly round that unloads every van at once.

Quarantine works locally: a depot can move units off its shelf into quarantine while a repeat screen is pending, and can release quarantined units back to the shelf when the screen comes back clean. Neither movement changes the total.

The action set is exactly: propose a transfer of a positive number of units from one depot to a different depot, when no proposal is outstanding and the sender's shelf covers it; cast a depot's vote on the outstanding proposal; execute the outstanding proposal once a strict majority has voted, moving the units onto a van bound for the destination; drop the outstanding proposal, discarding its votes; unload the van stock waiting for one depot onto that depot's shelf; run the nightly round that unloads every depot's van stock at once; move units from a depot's shelf into quarantine; and release quarantined units back onto the shelf.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of units on depot shelves, in quarantine, and in transit on vans is always exactly the stock the service is accountable for.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Stock never stays on a van forever — whenever any depot has stock in transit, every depot's in-transit stock is eventually unloaded onto its shelf.

---- MODULE W4Od17m4p0t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Bags, QueueDepth

\* Induction is a bounded FIFO: refusing to enqueue at the depth limit is the
\* backpressure that stalls the check-in belts.
\* The screening lane is the critical resource and its interlock names the one bag it
\* is indexed on; the supervisor's override skips the queue but not the interlock.
\* The invariant is that lane occupancy and the interlock never disagree.

Open == "open"

VARIABLES induct, lane, interlock, cleared, hot
vars == <<induct, lane, interlock, cleared, hot>>

Queued(b) == \E i \in 1..Len(induct) : induct[i] = b

TypeOK ==
  /\ induct \in Seq(Bags)
  /\ lane \subseteq Bags
  /\ interlock \in Bags \cup {Open}
  /\ cleared \subseteq Bags
  /\ hot \subseteq Bags

Init ==
  /\ induct = <<>>
  /\ lane = {}
  /\ interlock = Open
  /\ cleared = {}
  /\ hot = {}

InductBag(b) ==
  /\ ~Queued(b)
  /\ b \notin lane
  /\ b \notin cleared
  /\ Len(induct) < QueueDepth
  /\ induct' = Append(induct, b)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lane, interlock, cleared, hot>>

DrawFront ==
  /\ induct # <<>>
  /\ interlock = Open
  /\ interlock' = Head(induct)
  /\ lane' = lane \cup {Head(induct)}
  /\ induct' = Tail(induct)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cleared, hot>>

ReleaseBag ==
  /\ interlock # Open
  /\ interlock \in lane
  /\ lane' = lane \ {interlock}
  /\ cleared' = cleared \cup {interlock}
  /\ interlock' = Open
  /\ UNCHANGED <<induct, hot>>

SendToCarousel(b) ==
  /\ b \in cleared
  /\ cleared' = cleared \ {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<induct, lane, interlock, hot>>

FlagHot(b) ==
  /\ b \notin hot
  /\ hot' = hot \cup {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<induct, lane, interlock, cleared>>

SupervisorPlace(b) ==
  /\ b \in hot
  /\ interlock = Open
  /\ ~Queued(b)
  /\ b \notin lane
  /\ b \notin cleared
  /\ interlock' = b
  /\ lane' = lane \cup {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<induct, cleared, hot>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Bags : InductBag(b) \/ SendToCarousel(b) \/ FlagHot(b) \/ SupervisorPlace(b)
  \/ DrawFront
  \/ ReleaseBag

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

LaneMatchesInterlock == \A b \in lane : interlock = b
====

CONSTANTS
  Bags = {"bg1","bg2","bg3"}
  QueueDepth = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT LaneMatchesInterlock
nl:
An airport's outbound baggage system routes every checked bag through a single high-speed screening lane before it can go to a make-up carousel. The screening lane is the bottleneck and it is strictly one bag at a time: the machine's X-ray head indexes on a bag, images it, and releases it, and a second bag entering while the first is still inside produces an image the screening algorithm cannot attribute, which by regulation means both bags have to be pulled and hand-searched. The machine therefore carries a physical interlock that names the bag it is currently indexed on; the interlock is open when the lane is empty.

Bags reach the lane through a bounded induction queue. A bag that is not already queued, not in the lane, and not already cleared can be inducted while the queue is below its depth limit; once the queue is at the limit, induction is refused and the check-in belts back up, which is exactly the backpressure the designers intended. The lane draws from the front of the queue, and only when the interlock is open: taking a bag sets the interlock to that bag and puts the bag in the lane. When the machine releases a bag, the interlock is reopened and the bag joins the cleared set, from which it eventually leaves for its carousel.

The duty supervisor has an override for hot transfers — a bag off a late inbound with twenty minutes to its connection. She flags such a bag and can then lift it straight onto the screening lane, bypassing the induction queue entirely. What she cannot bypass is the interlock: she may only place a bag when the interlock is open, and placing it sets the interlock to that bag exactly as a normal draw would. The override buys the bag a place in the order, not an exemption from the machine.

The action set is exactly: induct a bag that is unqueued, not in the lane and not cleared, while the queue is below its depth limit; draw the front of the queue into the lane when the interlock is open, setting the interlock to that bag; release the bag the interlock names, reopening the interlock and adding the bag to the cleared set; send a cleared bag off to its carousel, removing it from the cleared set; flag a bag as a hot transfer; and use the supervisor's override to place a flagged, unqueued, uncleared bag directly onto the lane when the interlock is open.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every bag inside the screening lane is the bag the machine's interlock names, so the lane never holds two bags at once.

---- MODULE W4Od1m9p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Desks, Slots, PoolSizes, MaxConfig, FirstPool

\* Two independently commissioned desks draw from one pool of landing slots.
\* A reconfiguration publishes the next configuration number together with the pool
\* size that applies from then on; a desk behind the published number is holding slots
\* the new pool may not cover, so adopting means surrendering them first.
\* The invariant bounds only the holdings that count -- those under the published number.

VARIABLES config, poolSize, held, deskConfig, swept
vars == <<config, poolSize, held, deskConfig, swept>>

CurrentHeld == UNION { IF deskConfig[k] = config THEN held[k] ELSE {} : k \in Desks }
Behind == { k \in Desks : deskConfig[k] # config }

TypeOK ==
  /\ config \in 0..MaxConfig
  /\ poolSize \in PoolSizes
  /\ held \in [Desks -> SUBSET Slots]
  /\ deskConfig \in [Desks -> 0..MaxConfig]
  /\ swept \subseteq Slots

Init ==
  /\ config = 0
  /\ poolSize = FirstPool
  /\ held = [k \in Desks |-> {}]
  /\ deskConfig = [k \in Desks |-> 0]
  /\ swept = {}

Republish(n) ==
  /\ config < MaxConfig
  /\ n \in PoolSizes
  /\ config' = config + 1
  /\ poolSize' = n
  /\ UNCHANGED <<held, deskConfig, swept>>

AdoptConfig(k) ==
  /\ deskConfig[k] # config
  /\ deskConfig' = [deskConfig EXCEPT ![k] = config]
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![k] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<config, poolSize, swept>>

TowerSweep ==
  /\ Behind # {}
  /\ deskConfig' = [k \in Desks |-> config]
  /\ held' = [k \in Desks |-> IF k \in Behind THEN {} ELSE held[k]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<config, poolSize, swept>>

TakeSlot(k, s) ==
  /\ deskConfig[k] = config
  /\ s \notin CurrentHeld
  /\ s \notin swept
  /\ Cardinality(CurrentHeld) < poolSize
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![k] = held[k] \cup {s}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<config, poolSize, deskConfig, swept>>

LandAircraft(k, s) ==
  /\ s \in held[k]
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![k] = held[k] \ {s}]
  /\ swept' = swept \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<config, poolSize, deskConfig>>

ReportClean(s) ==
  /\ s \in swept
  /\ swept' = swept \ {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<config, poolSize, held, deskConfig>>

HandBack(k, s) ==
  /\ s \in held[k]
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![k] = held[k] \ {s}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<config, poolSize, deskConfig, swept>>

Next ==
  \/ \E n \in PoolSizes : Republish(n)
  \/ \E k \in Desks : AdoptConfig(k)
  \/ \E k \in Desks, s \in Slots : TakeSlot(k, s) \/ LandAircraft(k, s) \/ HandBack(k, s)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : ReportClean(s)
  \/ TowerSweep

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(TowerSweep)

PoolNeverOversubscribed == Cardinality(CurrentHeld) =< poolSize

DesksCatchUp == (Behind # {}) ~> (Behind = {})
====
nl:
A busy airport is worked by two approach control positions — the north arrivals desk and the south arrivals desk — that were commissioned years apart and run on separate consoles. They are independent in every respect except one: they draw landing slots from a single shared pool for the same runway complex, and the pool has a hard size. Only so many aircraft can be committed to final approach at once, and the number depends on which runway configuration is in force.

The runway configuration changes during the day. A wind shift, a closure for a rubber removal crew, a switch to reduced separation in good visibility — each of these is published as a reconfiguration under the next configuration number, and each publication comes with the pool size that applies from then on. Because a reconfiguration can shrink the pool, slots that were granted under the previous configuration cannot simply be carried across; a desk that is still working to a superseded configuration is holding slots that the new configuration may not have room for. So a desk that finds itself behind the published configuration adopts the new one, which means surrendering everything it was holding and starting again under the new number. The two desks adopt independently, and the tower also runs a sweep that pulls every desk that is behind onto the published configuration in one go.

A desk that is working to the published configuration may take a free slot from the pool for an inbound aircraft, provided the pool still has room counting the slots both desks are holding under the published configuration. When an aircraft lands the desk gives its slot back and the slot goes onto the swept list until the runway crew reports it clean, after which it returns to the pool. A desk may also hand a slot back without a landing, when an aircraft goes around or diverts.

The action set is exactly: publish a reconfiguration under the next configuration number with a new pool size; have one desk adopt the published configuration, surrendering the slots it held under the old one; run the tower sweep that brings every behind desk onto the published configuration, surrendering their held slots; take a free slot for a desk that is working to the published configuration, when the pool has room; land an aircraft, releasing its slot onto the swept list; report a swept slot clean, returning it to the pool; and hand a slot back without a landing.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of slots held under the currently published configuration, counting both desks together, never exceeds the pool size that configuration published.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever a desk is working to a superseded configuration, both desks eventually end up working to the published one.

---- MODULE W4Od17m2p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Bags, Parties, SheetLines, Allowances

\* Two-phase commit across the make-up crew and load control; preparing is reversible,
\* writing the manifest line is not.
\* The hold allowance is republished during the turnaround, so the capacity test is
\* taken at prepare time against whatever is in force then.
\* The invariant is the two-way tag/manifest reconciliation that a double write breaks.

Unstamped == 0

VARIABLES manifest, tagLine, stage, votes, allowance
vars == <<manifest, tagLine, stage, votes, allowance>>

Stages == {"idle", "voting", "prepared"}

TypeOK ==
  /\ manifest \in Seq(Bags)
  /\ tagLine \in [Bags -> 0..SheetLines]
  /\ stage \in [Bags -> Stages]
  /\ votes \in [Bags -> SUBSET Parties]
  /\ allowance \in Allowances

Init ==
  /\ manifest = <<>>
  /\ tagLine = [b \in Bags |-> Unstamped]
  /\ stage = [b \in Bags |-> "idle"]
  /\ votes = [b \in Bags |-> {}]
  /\ allowance \in Allowances

BeginLoad(b) ==
  /\ stage[b] = "idle"
  /\ tagLine[b] = Unstamped
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![b] = "voting"]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![b] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<manifest, tagLine, allowance>>

RecordVote(b, p) ==
  /\ stage[b] = "voting"
  /\ p \notin votes[b]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![b] = votes[b] \cup {p}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<manifest, tagLine, stage, allowance>>

PrepareBag(b) ==
  /\ stage[b] = "voting"
  /\ votes[b] = Parties
  /\ Len(manifest) < allowance
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![b] = "prepared"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<manifest, tagLine, votes, allowance>>

WriteLine(b) ==
  /\ stage[b] = "prepared"
  /\ tagLine[b] = Unstamped
  /\ Len(manifest) < SheetLines
  /\ manifest' = Append(manifest, b)
  /\ tagLine' = [tagLine EXCEPT ![b] = Len(manifest) + 1]
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![b] = "idle"]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![b] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED allowance

AbandonBag(b) ==
  /\ stage[b] \in {"voting", "prepared"}
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![b] = "idle"]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![b] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<manifest, tagLine, allowance>>

Republish(a) ==
  /\ a \in Allowances
  /\ a # allowance
  /\ allowance' = a
  /\ UNCHANGED <<manifest, tagLine, stage, votes>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Bags : BeginLoad(b) \/ PrepareBag(b) \/ WriteLine(b) \/ AbandonBag(b)
  \/ \E b \in Bags, p \in Parties : RecordVote(b, p)
  \/ \E a \in Allowances : Republish(a)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TagsReconcileWithSheet ==
  /\ \A b \in Bags :
       tagLine[b] # Unstamped => (tagLine[b] =< Len(manifest) /\ manifest[tagLine[b]] = b)
  /\ \A i \in 1..Len(manifest) : tagLine[manifest[i]] = i
====
nl:
Bags routed to a departing aircraft do not go into the hold on anyone's say-so. Committing a bag to the load involves the make-up crew, who have the bag on the trailer, and load control, who own the aircraft's weight and balance. The two must agree, so each bag is committed as a two-phase commit: the bag goes out for voting, each party records its vote, and when both have voted the bag is prepared. Preparing is still reversible; the bag can be pulled off the trailer and the transaction abandoned.

What is not reversible is writing the bag onto the load manifest. The manifest is the sheet that goes to the captain, and it is written one line at a time and never erased. Each line records a bag, and the tag on the bag itself is stamped with the line number it went onto. That pairing is the whole audit: a tag whose line number does not lead back to that same bag, or a manifest line whose bag does not carry that line's number, means the reconciliation between the ramp and the flight deck has broken. In practice the way it breaks is a bag written onto the manifest twice, which leaves the earlier line orphaned — its bag now carries the later line number — and makes the hold count disagree with the sheet.

The hold's allowance is not fixed while the turnaround is running. Load control recalculates as the fuel figure firms up and as freight is added or pulled, and each recalculation republishes the number of bags the hold will take. A bag is only allowed to prepare if the manifest is still short of the allowance currently in force, so an allowance that drops mid-turnaround stops further bags from preparing without touching the ones already written. The manifest sheet itself has a fixed number of lines.

The action set is exactly: begin a load transaction for a bag that is idle and not already manifested; record a party's vote on a bag that is out for voting; prepare a bag once both parties have voted and the manifest is still short of the current allowance; write a prepared bag onto the next manifest line, stamping that line number onto its tag, while the sheet has lines left; abandon a bag that is voting or prepared, returning it to idle; and republish a different hold allowance.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every bag tag stamped with a manifest line number leads back to a manifest line holding that same bag, and every manifest line holds a bag whose tag carries that line's number, so no bag is ever written onto the manifest twice.

---- MODULE W4Od8m2p6t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Students, Offices, MaxTerm

\* Two-phase commit across the offices that must agree before a seat is spoken for.
\* The dean's signature can stand in for an office's vote, but the currency checks --
\* published term, no registration hold -- are applied at prepare time, so an override
\* cannot smuggle a stale or unauthorised enrolment past them.

VARIABLES term, stage, openedIn, votes, holds, enrolled
vars == <<term, stage, openedIn, votes, holds, enrolled>>

Stages == {"idle", "voting", "prepared"}
InFlight == { s \in Students : stage[s] # "idle" }

TypeOK ==
  /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
  /\ stage \in [Students -> Stages]
  /\ openedIn \in [Students -> 0..MaxTerm]
  /\ votes \in [Students -> SUBSET Offices]
  /\ holds \subseteq Students
  /\ enrolled \subseteq Students

Init ==
  /\ term = 0
  /\ stage = [s \in Students |-> "idle"]
  /\ openedIn = [s \in Students |-> 0]
  /\ votes = [s \in Students |-> {}]
  /\ holds = {}
  /\ enrolled = {}

OpenEnrolment(s) ==
  /\ stage[s] = "idle"
  /\ s \notin holds
  /\ s \notin enrolled
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![s] = "voting"]
  /\ openedIn' = [openedIn EXCEPT ![s] = term]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, holds, enrolled>>

OfficeVote(s, o) ==
  /\ stage[s] = "voting"
  /\ o \notin votes[s]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = votes[s] \cup {o}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, stage, openedIn, holds, enrolled>>

DeanSignoff(s, o) ==
  /\ stage[s] = "voting"
  /\ o \notin votes[s]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = votes[s] \cup {o}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, stage, openedIn, holds, enrolled>>

PrepareEnrolment(s) ==
  /\ stage[s] = "voting"
  /\ votes[s] = Offices
  /\ openedIn[s] = term
  /\ s \notin holds
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![s] = "prepared"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, openedIn, votes, holds, enrolled>>

CommitEnrolment(s) ==
  /\ stage[s] = "prepared"
  /\ enrolled' = enrolled \cup {s}
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![s] = "idle"]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, openedIn, holds>>

Abandon(s) ==
  /\ stage[s] # "idle"
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![s] = "idle"]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, openedIn, holds, enrolled>>

RollTerm ==
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ stage' = [s \in Students |-> "idle"]
  /\ votes' = [s \in Students |-> {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<openedIn, holds, enrolled>>

PlaceHold(s) ==
  /\ s \notin holds
  /\ holds' = holds \cup {s}
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![s] = "idle"]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, openedIn, enrolled>>

HoldClinic ==
  /\ holds # {}
  /\ holds' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, stage, openedIn, votes, enrolled>>

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Students : OpenEnrolment(s) \/ PrepareEnrolment(s)
       \/ CommitEnrolment(s) \/ Abandon(s) \/ PlaceHold(s)
  \/ \E s \in Students, o \in Offices : OfficeVote(s, o) \/ DeanSignoff(s, o)
  \/ RollTerm
  \/ HoldClinic

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(HoldClinic)

PreparedEnrolmentsAreCurrent ==
  \A s \in Students :
    stage[s] = "prepared" => (openedIn[s] = term /\ votes[s] = Offices /\ s \notin holds)

HoldsNeverStick == (holds # {}) ~> (holds = {})
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Students = {"sa","sb"}
  Offices = {"dept","bursar"}
  MaxTerm = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT PreparedEnrolmentsAreCurrent
PROPERTY HoldsNeverStick
nl:
A university enrols students into capped courses through a registration engine that will not act on any single office's word. Each enrolment runs as a two-phase commit across the offices that have a say: the department, which owns the seat, and the bursar, who owns the money. A student's enrolment opens for voting, each office records its vote, and only when every office has voted does the enrolment become prepared — the point at which the seat is genuinely spoken for and the commit will go through.

Two things make a vote worthless. The first is the registration term. Registration runs in terms, and each term is published under a number; when the registration period rolls over, the number advances and everything opened under the old number is stale, because the seat counts, the prerequisites and the fee schedule have all been recomputed. An enrolment opened in a superseded term must not be allowed to reach the prepared state, and rolling the term therefore knocks every enrolment in flight back to idle. The second is a registration hold. The bursar places a hold on a student with unpaid fees, and a student under a hold is not an authorised party to any enrolment; placing a hold knocks that student's enrolment in flight back to idle, and no enrolment for a held student may prepare.

The dean's office has an override, and it is a real one: the dean can sign off on an office's behalf, and that signature is recorded as that office's vote. This is how a student gets enrolled when a department head is on sabbatical and nobody else can sign. What the dean's signature does not do is make a stale enrolment current or make a held student authorised — those checks are applied when the enrolment prepares, not when the votes are gathered. The dean's office also runs the hold clinic, which clears every outstanding registration hold at once; that is the route by which a student who has been blocked gets back into the process.

The action set is exactly: open an enrolment for a student who is idle, unheld and not already enrolled, tagging it with the published term; record an office's own vote on an enrolment that is out for voting; record the dean's signature as an office's vote on an enrolment that is out for voting; prepare an enrolment whose votes are complete, whose tagged term is the published one, and whose student is unheld; commit a prepared enrolment, enrolling the student; abandon an enrolment that is voting or prepared; roll the registration term, knocking every enrolment in flight back to idle; place a registration hold on a student, knocking their enrolment in flight back to idle; and run the dean's hold clinic, clearing every outstanding hold.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any enrolment that has reached the prepared state carries the published term number, has a vote recorded from every office, and belongs to a student who is not under a registration hold.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Registration holds never block a student permanently — whenever any hold is outstanding, the dean's hold clinic eventually leaves no hold outstanding.

---- MODULE W4Od4m6p4t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Vehicles, Bays, DwellSpan, Figures

\* A bay is granted for a bounded dwell that lapses on its own; the sweep is what
\* recovers a bay from a vehicle nobody came back for.
\* The reclaim figure is republished while the site runs and a reduction is refused
\* while it would sit below the bays already drawing water.
\* The invariant is that draw never outruns the figure currently published.

NoVehicle == "none"

VARIABLES lessee, dwell, figure, waiting, apron
vars == <<lessee, dwell, figure, waiting, apron>>

Running == { y \in Bays : lessee[y] # NoVehicle }
Lapsed == { y \in Bays : lessee[y] # NoVehicle /\ dwell[y] = 0 }

TypeOK ==
  /\ lessee \in [Bays -> Vehicles \cup {NoVehicle}]
  /\ dwell \in [Bays -> 0..DwellSpan]
  /\ figure \in Figures
  /\ waiting \subseteq Vehicles
  /\ apron \subseteq Vehicles

Init ==
  /\ lessee = [y \in Bays |-> NoVehicle]
  /\ dwell = [y \in Bays |-> 0]
  /\ figure \in Figures
  /\ waiting = {}
  /\ apron = {}

JoinQueue(v) ==
  /\ v \notin waiting
  /\ v \notin apron
  /\ \A y \in Bays : lessee[y] # v
  /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {v}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lessee, dwell, figure, apron>>

GrantBay(y, v) ==
  /\ v \in waiting
  /\ lessee[y] = NoVehicle
  /\ Cardinality(Running) < figure
  /\ lessee' = [lessee EXCEPT ![y] = v]
  /\ dwell' = [dwell EXCEPT ![y] = DwellSpan]
  /\ waiting' = waiting \ {v}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<figure, apron>>

TickDwell ==
  /\ \E y \in Bays : lessee[y] # NoVehicle /\ dwell[y] > 0
  /\ dwell' = [y \in Bays |->
                 IF lessee[y] # NoVehicle /\ dwell[y] > 0 THEN dwell[y] - 1 ELSE dwell[y]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lessee, figure, waiting, apron>>

SweepLapsed ==
  /\ Lapsed # {}
  /\ lessee' = [y \in Bays |-> IF y \in Lapsed THEN NoVehicle ELSE lessee[y]]
  /\ apron' = apron \cup { lessee[y] : y \in Lapsed }
  /\ UNCHANGED <<dwell, figure, waiting>>

TopUp(y) ==
  /\ lessee[y] # NoVehicle
  /\ dwell[y] < DwellSpan
  /\ dwell' = [dwell EXCEPT ![y] = DwellSpan]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lessee, figure, waiting, apron>>

Republish(n) ==
  /\ n \in Figures
  /\ n # figure
  /\ Cardinality(Running) =< n
  /\ figure' = n
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lessee, dwell, waiting, apron>>

DriveOff(v) ==
  /\ v \in apron
  /\ apron' = apron \ {v}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lessee, dwell, figure, waiting>>

Next ==
  \/ \E v \in Vehicles : JoinQueue(v) \/ DriveOff(v)
  \/ \E y \in Bays, v \in Vehicles : GrantBay(y, v)
  \/ \E y \in Bays : TopUp(y)
  \/ TickDwell
  \/ SweepLapsed
  \/ \E n \in Figures : Republish(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ReclaimFigureHonored == Cardinality(Running) =< figure
====
nl:
A car wash runs several treatment bays off one water reclaim plant. A vehicle does not simply drive into a bay; the site controller grants it a bay for a bounded dwell, after which the grant lapses on its own. The dwell exists because vehicles get abandoned mid-wash — a driver walks off to the coffee machine, a van stalls — and a bay whose grant has lapsed is taken back and the vehicle pushed out to the finished apron whether or not anyone came back for it. A vehicle that is still being worked on can have its dwell topped back up to a full span while it is in the bay.

The binding constraint is not the number of bays but the reclaim plant. Running a bay draws recovered water, and the plant will only support so many bays running at once. That number is not fixed for the day: the plant controller republishes it as the settling tanks fill and empty, as the filter backwash cycle runs, and as the local water authority's restrictions come and go. The number of bays running is checked against whatever figure is currently published, at the moment a bay is granted.

Republishing a lower figure is where the site has to be careful. The plant controller is not permitted to publish a figure below the number of bays already running — it would mean the plant was already over-drawing the instant the figure took effect, and the reclaim loop would run dry. So a reduction waits until enough bays have lapsed or finished, and only then takes effect. Raising the figure has no such constraint.

The action set is exactly: a vehicle joins the waiting queue; the controller grants a waiting vehicle a free bay at a full dwell, provided the number of running bays is below the published figure; the dwell clock ticks down on every running bay that has time left; the controller sweeps every bay whose dwell has lapsed, freeing it and pushing its vehicle out to the finished apron; a vehicle in a bay has its dwell topped back up to a full span; the plant controller republishes a different figure, provided it is not below the number of bays already running; and a vehicle on the finished apron drives off the site.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of bays running at any moment never exceeds the reclaim figure currently published by the plant controller.

---- MODULE W4Od4m6p6t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Vehicles, Bays, MaxSequence

\* A ticket is a lease on the line plan: it carries the sequencing number in force when
\* it was stamped, and re-sequencing expires every outstanding ticket at once.
\* Because tickets expire in place, the line halts and is cleared before it restarts;
\* the invariant only bites on a running line, which is what makes the clear-then-restart
\* discipline load-bearing rather than decorative.

Empty == "empty"

VARIABLES running, sequence, occupant, ticket, inService
vars == <<running, sequence, occupant, ticket, inService>>

Occupied == { y \in Bays : occupant[y] # Empty }

TypeOK ==
  /\ running \in BOOLEAN
  /\ sequence \in 0..MaxSequence
  /\ occupant \in [Bays -> Vehicles \cup {Empty}]
  /\ ticket \in [Vehicles -> 0..MaxSequence]
  /\ inService \subseteq Bays

Init ==
  /\ running = TRUE
  /\ sequence = 0
  /\ occupant = [y \in Bays |-> Empty]
  /\ ticket = [v \in Vehicles |-> 0]
  /\ inService = Bays

Resequence(g) ==
  /\ running
  /\ sequence < MaxSequence
  /\ g # {}
  /\ sequence' = sequence + 1
  /\ inService' = g
  /\ running' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occupant, ticket>>

ClearLine ==
  /\ ~running
  /\ Occupied # {}
  /\ occupant' = [y \in Bays |-> Empty]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<running, sequence, ticket, inService>>

RestartLine ==
  /\ ~running
  /\ Occupied = {}
  /\ running' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sequence, occupant, ticket, inService>>

Restamp(v) ==
  /\ ticket[v] # sequence
  /\ \A y \in Bays : occupant[y] # v
  /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![v] = sequence]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<running, sequence, occupant, inService>>

PullIn(y, v) ==
  /\ running
  /\ y \in inService
  /\ occupant[y] = Empty
  /\ ticket[v] = sequence
  /\ \A z \in Bays : occupant[z] # v
  /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![y] = v]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<running, sequence, ticket, inService>>

FinishWash(y) ==
  /\ running
  /\ occupant[y] # Empty
  /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![y] = Empty]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<running, sequence, ticket, inService>>

Next ==
  \/ \E g \in SUBSET Bays : Resequence(g)
  \/ \E v \in Vehicles : Restamp(v)
  \/ \E y \in Bays, v \in Vehicles : PullIn(y, v)
  \/ \E y \in Bays : FinishWash(y)
  \/ ClearLine
  \/ RestartLine

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(ClearLine)
  /\ WF_vars(RestartLine)

NoStaleTreatment ==
  running => \A y \in Bays : occupant[y] # Empty => ticket[occupant[y]] = sequence

HaltsAlwaysEnd == (~running) ~> running
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Vehicles = {"w1","w2"}
  Bays = {"y1","y2"}
  MaxSequence = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoStaleTreatment
PROPERTY HaltsAlwaysEnd
nl:
A conveyor car wash issues each vehicle a chain ticket before it may be pulled into a treatment bay. The ticket is not just an identifier: it is stamped with the sequencing number of the line plan in force when the ticket was issued, and it is the sequencing number that tells every bay what chemical programme, what brush pressure and what dwell to apply to the vehicle it is holding.

The line plan is re-sequenced during the day. Bays are dropped out of service for chemical refills and brought back in; the mix in the pre-soak tank is changed for the salt season; a bay's dryer is swapped. Each of these is published as a re-sequence: it advances the sequencing number and names the set of bays that are in service from then on, which is how the line's working capacity changes while vehicles are already on site. Re-sequencing halts the line, because every ticket issued under the old number is now stale — a bay applying the old programme to a vehicle whose plan has been superseded is exactly how a matt-wrapped car gets a brush wash.

While the line is halted, the crew clears it: every occupied bay is emptied and its vehicle pushed back into the holding lane. The line is only restarted once every bay is empty, so no vehicle can be sitting in a bay under a stale ticket when the conveyor starts moving again. Vehicles in the holding lane get their tickets re-stamped with the current sequencing number, and only a vehicle whose ticket carries the current number may be pulled into an in-service bay, and only while the line is running and the bay is free. When a wash finishes the bay is emptied back to the lane.

The action set is exactly: re-sequence the line while it is running, advancing the sequencing number, naming a new non-empty set of in-service bays, and halting the line; clear the line while it is halted, emptying every occupied bay back into the holding lane; restart the halted line once every bay is empty; re-stamp a vehicle's ticket with the current sequencing number; pull a vehicle whose ticket is current into a free in-service bay while the line is running; and finish a wash, emptying that bay back into the lane.

SAFETY PROPERTY: While the line is running, every vehicle sitting in a bay holds a ticket stamped with the current sequencing number, so no bay ever treats a vehicle under a superseded line plan.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: A halt is never permanent — whenever the line has been halted for a re-sequence, it eventually returns to running.

---- MODULE W4Od14m6p4t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Drones, Bands, AirtimeSpan, MaxSlots

\* Airtime is a lease: a drone that has lost its command link is dropped off air by the
\* sweep rather than holding a band slot forever.
\* Slot counts are per band and are re-cut during the incident; a cut re-tasks the band,
\* dropping everyone on it in the same move, so the count is never left over-subscribed.
\* The invariant is per band, not global -- each band is checked against its own count.

OffAir == "offair"

VARIABLES onBand, airtime, slots, requested
vars == <<onBand, airtime, slots, requested>>

Streaming(b) == { d \in Drones : onBand[d] = b }
Lapsed == { d \in Drones : onBand[d] # OffAir /\ airtime[d] = 0 }

TypeOK ==
  /\ onBand \in [Drones -> Bands \cup {OffAir}]
  /\ airtime \in [Drones -> 0..AirtimeSpan]
  /\ slots \in [Bands -> 0..MaxSlots]
  /\ requested \subseteq Drones

Init ==
  /\ onBand = [d \in Drones |-> OffAir]
  /\ airtime = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
  /\ slots = [b \in Bands |-> MaxSlots]
  /\ requested = {}

RequestDrone(d) ==
  /\ onBand[d] = OffAir
  /\ d \notin requested
  /\ requested' = requested \cup {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onBand, airtime, slots>>

ClearOnto(d, b) ==
  /\ d \in requested
  /\ onBand[d] = OffAir
  /\ Cardinality(Streaming(b)) < slots[b]
  /\ onBand' = [onBand EXCEPT ![d] = b]
  /\ airtime' = [airtime EXCEPT ![d] = AirtimeSpan]
  /\ requested' = requested \ {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED slots

TickAirtime ==
  /\ \E d \in Drones : onBand[d] # OffAir /\ airtime[d] > 0
  /\ airtime' = [d \in Drones |->
                   IF onBand[d] # OffAir /\ airtime[d] > 0 THEN airtime[d] - 1 ELSE airtime[d]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onBand, slots, requested>>

SweepLapsed ==
  /\ Lapsed # {}
  /\ onBand' = [d \in Drones |-> IF d \in Lapsed THEN OffAir ELSE onBand[d]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<airtime, slots, requested>>

ExtendAirtime(d) ==
  /\ onBand[d] # OffAir
  /\ airtime[d] < AirtimeSpan
  /\ airtime' = [airtime EXCEPT ![d] = AirtimeSpan]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onBand, slots, requested>>

RaiseSlots(b, n) ==
  /\ n \in 0..MaxSlots
  /\ n > slots[b]
  /\ slots' = [slots EXCEPT ![b] = n]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onBand, airtime, requested>>

RetaskBand(b, n) ==
  /\ n \in 0..MaxSlots
  /\ n < slots[b]
  /\ onBand' = [d \in Drones |-> IF onBand[d] = b THEN OffAir ELSE onBand[d]]
  /\ slots' = [slots EXCEPT ![b] = n]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<airtime, requested>>

Next ==
  \/ \E d \in Drones : RequestDrone(d) \/ ExtendAirtime(d)
  \/ \E d \in Drones, b \in Bands : ClearOnto(d, b)
  \/ \E b \in Bands, n \in 0..MaxSlots : RaiseSlots(b, n) \/ RetaskBand(b, n)
  \/ TickAirtime
  \/ SweepLapsed

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BandSlotsHonored == \A b \in Bands : Cardinality(Streaming(b)) =< slots[b]
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Drones = {"dr1","dr2","dr3"}
  Bands = {"vhf","uhf"}
  AirtimeSpan = 1
  MaxSlots = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT BandSlotsHonored
nl:
A wildfire surveillance swarm flies persistent infrared coverage over an incident. Every drone aloft streams live video to the ground station, and every stream has to ride one of the station's downlink bands. A drone is cleared onto a band for a bounded airtime; that clearance is a lease and it runs out on its own, because a drone that loses its command link keeps flying its last pattern and would otherwise hold a band's slot indefinitely. When a lease runs out the station drops that drone off air, and the drone's slot on the band comes back. A drone still under command has its airtime extended before it lapses.

Each band has its own slot count, and the counts are not fixed for the incident. The communications officer reallocates bandwidth as the fire moves: a band gets more slots when the air attack supervisor needs more eyes on the head of the fire, and gets fewer when spectrum is handed to the retardant ships or to the sheriff's channel. Raising a band's slot count is straightforward. Cutting it is not, and the station does not attempt to be clever about it: cutting a band's slot count re-tasks the band outright, dropping every drone currently on it off air in one move, and only then does the reduced count take effect. Those drones fall back to the launch request pool and have to be cleared onto a band again.

A drone is only cleared onto a band after the incident commander has requested it, and only while the band still has a free slot under the count currently in force. A drone that has been dropped off air, whether by lapse or by re-tasking, can be requested again.

The action set is exactly: request a drone that is off air and not already requested; clear a requested off-air drone onto a band that has a free slot under its current count, at full airtime; tick the airtime clock down on every drone aloft that has time left; sweep every drone whose airtime has lapsed, dropping it off air; extend a drone's airtime back to full while it is aloft; raise a band's slot count; and re-task a band to a lower slot count, dropping every drone on it off air as part of the same move.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every downlink band, the number of drones streaming on that band never exceeds the slot count currently in force for that band.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od12m9p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Units, Fridges, PlanFigures, MaxPlan, FirstFigure

\* Publishing the next plan number pulls the whole inventory onto the trolley, so the
\* per-fridge figure only ever has to hold units shelved under the current plan.
\* A re-shelving round places the entire trolley in one pass, choosing any allocation
\* that respects the figure; figures are always large enough for the whole inventory.
\* The invariant is the census: shelves pairwise disjoint, disjoint from the trolley,
\* and together covering every unit.

VARIABLES plan, figure, shelved, trolley, shelvedUnder
vars == <<plan, figure, shelved, trolley, shelvedUnder>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ plan \in 0..MaxPlan
  /\ figure \in PlanFigures
  /\ shelved \in [Fridges -> SUBSET Units]
  /\ trolley \subseteq Units
  /\ shelvedUnder \in [Units -> 0..MaxPlan]

Init ==
  /\ plan = 0
  /\ figure = FirstFigure
  /\ shelved = [f \in Fridges |-> {}]
  /\ trolley = Units
  /\ shelvedUnder = [u \in Units |-> 0]

PublishPlan(n) ==
  /\ plan < MaxPlan
  /\ n \in PlanFigures
  /\ plan' = plan + 1
  /\ figure' = n
  /\ shelved' = [f \in Fridges |-> {}]
  /\ trolley' = Units
  /\ UNCHANGED shelvedUnder

ReshelveRound ==
  /\ trolley # {}
  /\ \E place \in [trolley -> Fridges] :
       /\ \A f \in Fridges :
            Cardinality(shelved[f]) + Cardinality({u \in trolley : place[u] = f}) =< figure
       /\ shelved' = [f \in Fridges |-> shelved[f] \cup {u \in trolley : place[u] = f}]
  /\ trolley' = {}
  /\ shelvedUnder' = [u \in Units |-> IF u \in trolley THEN plan ELSE shelvedUnder[u]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, figure>>

ShelveOne(u, f) ==
  /\ u \in trolley
  /\ Cardinality(shelved[f]) < figure
  /\ shelved' = [shelved EXCEPT ![f] = shelved[f] \cup {u}]
  /\ trolley' = trolley \ {u}
  /\ shelvedUnder' = [shelvedUnder EXCEPT ![u] = plan]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, figure>>

PullOne(u, f) ==
  /\ u \in shelved[f]
  /\ shelved' = [shelved EXCEPT ![f] = shelved[f] \ {u}]
  /\ trolley' = trolley \cup {u}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, figure, shelvedUnder>>

Next ==
  \/ \E n \in PlanFigures : PublishPlan(n)
  \/ \E u \in Units, f \in Fridges : ShelveOne(u, f) \/ PullOne(u, f)
  \/ ReshelveRound

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(ReshelveRound)

CensusCloses ==
  /\ (UNION { shelved[f] : f \in Fridges }) \cup trolley = Units
  /\ \A f \in Fridges : shelved[f] \cap trolley = {}
  /\ \A f, g \in Fridges : f # g => shelved[f] \cap shelved[g] = {}

TrolleyAlwaysEmpties == (trolley # {}) ~> (trolley = {})
====
nl:
A hospital blood bank keeps its inventory in a set of monitored fridges, and the arrangement of that inventory is governed by a storage plan. The plan says how many units a single fridge shelf assembly may hold — a figure that moves with the fridge model in use, the shelf inserts fitted, and the standing order in force for reserved capacity. Whenever any of that changes, the bank publishes a new storage plan under the next plan number.

Republishing a plan is disruptive on purpose. Every unit in the bank has to be re-shelved under the new plan, because the plan is what the audit reconciles against, and a unit sitting on a shelf under a superseded plan number cannot be shown to be stored correctly. So publishing a new plan pulls every unit out of the fridges and onto the transfer trolley in one move, and the units are then re-shelved under the new plan and the new per-fridge figure.

Re-shelving happens as a round: the technician takes the whole trolley and distributes every unit on it across the fridges in one pass, choosing any allocation that keeps each fridge within the figure the current plan publishes. Individual units can also be shelved one at a time into a fridge with room, and a unit can be pulled off a shelf back onto the trolley — for a crossmatch, for a temperature excursion check, for a label reprint. A unit shelved by either route records the plan number it was shelved under.

Whatever route is taken, the census must close. Every unit the bank holds is either on exactly one fridge's shelves or on the trolley — never on two fridges' shelves at once, never both shelved and on the trolley, and never absent from both. That is what the regulator counts, and the bank's storage plans are only ever published with a per-fridge figure large enough that the fridges between them can hold the whole inventory, so a re-shelving round can always be completed.

The action set is exactly: publish the next storage plan with a new per-fridge figure, pulling every unit onto the trolley; run a re-shelving round that distributes the whole trolley across the fridges within the current figure; shelve one unit from the trolley into a fridge that has room; and pull one unit off a fridge shelf back onto the trolley.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every unit in the bank is accounted for exactly once — the fridges' shelved sets are pairwise disjoint, none of them overlaps the trolley, and together with the trolley they cover the whole inventory.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: The trolley never stays loaded — whenever any unit is sitting on the transfer trolley, the bank eventually reaches a state in which the trolley is empty.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od0m8p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Schedulers, NumBlocks, RoomsPerBlock

\* Coarse before fine: a block is taken first, then rooms inside it, and a case may only
\* run where the scheduler holds both levels.
\* Two independently procured schedulers draw from the same room pool, so the two-level
\* holding is the only thing keeping them apart.
\* The invariant ties a running case to both levels of holding at once.

Blocks == 1..NumBlocks
Rooms == 1..(NumBlocks * RoomsPerBlock)
BlockOf(r) == ((r - 1) \div RoomsPerBlock) + 1
Nobody == "nobody"

VARIABLES blockHeld, roomHeld, running, queued, turnover
vars == <<blockHeld, roomHeld, running, queued, turnover>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ blockHeld \in [Blocks -> Schedulers \cup {Nobody}]
  /\ roomHeld \in [Rooms -> Schedulers \cup {Nobody}]
  /\ running \in [Schedulers -> SUBSET Rooms]
  /\ queued \in [Schedulers -> SUBSET Rooms]
  /\ turnover \subseteq Rooms

Init ==
  /\ blockHeld = [b \in Blocks |-> Nobody]
  /\ roomHeld = [r \in Rooms |-> Nobody]
  /\ running = [k \in Schedulers |-> {}]
  /\ queued = [k \in Schedulers |-> {}]
  /\ turnover = {}

TakeBlock(k, b) ==
  /\ blockHeld[b] = Nobody
  /\ blockHeld' = [blockHeld EXCEPT ![b] = k]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<roomHeld, running, queued, turnover>>

TakeRoom(k, r) ==
  /\ blockHeld[BlockOf(r)] = k
  /\ roomHeld[r] = Nobody
  /\ roomHeld' = [roomHeld EXCEPT ![r] = k]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<blockHeld, running, queued, turnover>>

QueueCase(k, r) ==
  /\ r \notin queued[k]
  /\ queued' = [queued EXCEPT ![k] = queued[k] \cup {r}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<blockHeld, roomHeld, running, turnover>>

StartCase(k, r) ==
  /\ r \in queued[k]
  /\ roomHeld[r] = k
  /\ blockHeld[BlockOf(r)] = k
  /\ r \notin turnover
  /\ r \notin running[k]
  /\ running' = [running EXCEPT ![k] = running[k] \cup {r}]
  /\ queued' = [queued EXCEPT ![k] = queued[k] \ {r}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<blockHeld, roomHeld, turnover>>

EndCase(k, r) ==
  /\ r \in running[k]
  /\ running' = [running EXCEPT ![k] = running[k] \ {r}]
  /\ turnover' = turnover \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<blockHeld, roomHeld, queued>>

CleaningDone(r) ==
  /\ r \in turnover
  /\ turnover' = turnover \ {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<blockHeld, roomHeld, running, queued>>

GiveBackRoom(k, r) ==
  /\ roomHeld[r] = k
  /\ r \notin running[k]
  /\ roomHeld' = [roomHeld EXCEPT ![r] = Nobody]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<blockHeld, running, queued, turnover>>

GiveBackBlock(k, b) ==
  /\ blockHeld[b] = k
  /\ \A r \in Rooms : BlockOf(r) = b => roomHeld[r] # k
  /\ blockHeld' = [blockHeld EXCEPT ![b] = Nobody]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<roomHeld, running, queued, turnover>>

Next ==
  \/ \E k \in Schedulers, b \in Blocks : TakeBlock(k, b) \/ GiveBackBlock(k, b)
  \/ \E k \in Schedulers, r \in Rooms :
       TakeRoom(k, r) \/ QueueCase(k, r) \/ StartCase(k, r) \/ EndCase(k, r)
         \/ GiveBackRoom(k, r)
  \/ \E r \in Rooms : CleaningDone(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CasesRunUnderBothHolds ==
  \A k \in Schedulers :
    \A r \in running[k] : roomHeld[r] = k /\ blockHeld[BlockOf(r)] = k
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Schedulers = {"elective","emergency"}
  NumBlocks = 2
  RoomsPerBlock = 1
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT CasesRunUnderBothHolds
nl:
A hospital's operating rooms are grouped into theatre blocks, and two scheduling systems draw cases from the same set of rooms. One is the elective scheduler, which plans lists weeks ahead; the other is the emergency scheduler, which is driven by the trauma pager. They were procured separately, they run on separate servers, and neither can see the other's list. What they do share is the rooms, and a room with two teams in it at once is the failure the whole arrangement exists to prevent: two patients wheeled to the same door, two anaesthetic machines, and a scrub team that cannot be told whose case is running.

Access is taken in two levels, coarse before fine. A scheduler first takes control of a whole theatre block; blocks are taken one at a time and a block under one scheduler's control cannot be taken by the other. Holding a block, the scheduler may then take an individual room inside that block, again one scheduler at a time per room. Only once a scheduler holds both the block and the room may it start a case in that room, and only for a room it has a case queued for. A scheduler may hold several rooms inside a block it controls and run cases in all of them.

Coming back out is the reverse. A case ends and the room goes into turnover for cleaning; a room in turnover cannot be entered until the cleaning is reported done. A scheduler gives a room back when it has no case running in it, and gives a block back only once it holds no rooms inside that block. Cases are queued against a room by whichever scheduler wants it, and a scheduler cannot start a case it has not queued.

The action set is exactly: take control of a free theatre block; take a free room inside a block the scheduler already controls; queue a case for a room; start a queued case in a room the scheduler holds inside a block it holds, when the room is not in turnover; end a case, putting that room into turnover; report the cleaning done, taking the room out of turnover; give back a room in which the scheduler has no case running; and give back a block in which the scheduler holds no rooms.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every room with a case running in it is held by the scheduler running that case, and the block containing that room is under that same scheduler's control, so two schedulers can never have cases running in the same room.
